purpose: Self-contained requirement and review provenance for the current development plan. Sources under dist are optional historical provenance; all substantive requirements, report text, original dispositions and task records needed for reconciliation are embedded here. Mapping or correcting a plan is not an implementation fix.

requirement_extraction.method: Every substantive normative r6 paragraph, product/class/work table row and the target SDK example block is preserved verbatim as one record; headings, table headers/separators, source-anchor lists and publication metadata are not requirements. The summaries are navigational and never narrow original_text except where a corrected disposition explicitly states the repair.

requirements.original_text: The deliverable is useful Iroha proof and privacy functionality, including **working RAM-LFE with all three program classes, verifiable output/identifier derivation, and threshold opening**. The user's instructions settle three design choices:
requirements.summary: Mandatory complete RAM-LFE and four binding user directions
requirements.rationale: Correct the three-versus-four wording; retain every binding direction and mandatory outcome.

requirements.original_text: 1. **Use each implemented capability immediately on testnet.** There are no activation transactions, qualification-signer keys, readiness certificates, lifecycle switches, all-protocol manifests, zero availability pins, audit signoffs or production-versus-integration chain-ID rules that determine whether a completed capability can run. Ordinary deployment makes implemented paths callable. Existing readiness machinery is removed as each affected path is rebuilt, across Core, Torii, SDKs, genesis and restore.
requirements.summary: Immediate independent usability without activation or review machinery
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: 2. **Make the best first-release design.** One current implementation, schema, relation and transcript per semantic role. Replace retired layouts, insecure backends and duplicate drivers directly; regenerate all consumers, fixtures and ABI V1 artifacts together. No compatibility aliases, old-verifier branches, fallback decoders, migration shims or second VM.
requirements.summary: Single first-release implementation and coherent consumer/schema/ABI retirement
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: 3. **Finish RAM-LFE.** Affine is the first usable slice. Bounded programs, genuine refresh, verifiable opening and threshold opening remain required. Failed experiments change the construction and work estimate; they do not turn RAM-LFE into signed receipts, ordinary plaintext computation, an OPRF-only substitute, an unavailable endpoint or an optional outcome.
requirements.summary: Affine first; bounded, genuine refresh, verifiable and threshold opening remain mandatory
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: 4. **One simple developer call for every supported operation.** Every listed algorithm has a native, typed ISI integration and a mandatory high-level SDK operation. The default call prepares, proves, signs, submits and returns the actual result; developers do not manually assemble crypto workflows. Each operation ships this surface with its implementation.
requirements.summary: Each implemented operation ships native typed ISI and one-call SDK result
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: This document is the sole normative plan. The [delivery graph](ZK%20plan%20r6%20delivery%20graph.md) is generated from its compact [dependency data](zk-plan-r6-graph.json); it holds artifact dependencies, not a second set of security rules. The [review reconciliation](ZK%20plan%20r6%20review%20reconciliation.md) maps all 133 earlier reviewer reports to the current requirements or explicit supersession. Archived reports are provenance, never execution instructions. Earlier repository specifications describe today's code and must be updated with the implementation; their retired activation proposals do not override these instructions.
requirements.summary: One tracked normative plan, graph and complete prior-report reconciliation
requirements.rationale: Replace optional dist normative links with the tracked current plan, graph and this self-contained reconciliation; old reports remain provenance.

requirements.original_text: **Proofs.** Consolidate the existing FASTPQ STARK machinery into one reusable owner with typed, semantically bound AIR descriptors. Use its real witness relations for execution, notes, credentials and FHE where specified. A public-data binding proof does not establish execution. A verifying-key upload cannot choose its own guarantee. Retain Halo2 and other mathematically distinct proof families where the product needs them; eliminating duplicate STARK drivers does not mean rewriting every proof system as STARK.
requirements.summary: Shared genuine FASTPQ machinery with mathematically distinct proof families retained
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: **FHE.** Build one exact modular RNS owner shared by RAM-LFE and SoraCloud. Keep arithmetic and codecs below policy, node and SDK layers. Create a dedicated `iroha_fhe` crate only for that real shared boundary; keep manifests/lockfile coherent and dependencies acyclic. RNS-BGV is the concrete starting candidate, with measured packing, noise, proof and sanitization work. No old degree-64 profile or scalar reconstruction helper becomes a secure RNS scheme by renaming it.
requirements.summary: Shared low-layer exact RNS ownership, concrete RNS-BGV candidate and secure construction
requirements.rationale: Include ZK-AMS in shared-arithmetic inventory while preserving distinct BGV/MKHE protocol semantics and independent test oracles.

requirements.original_text: **State and effects.** WG supplies a complete authenticated keyed State root and carried inclusion/absence/range witnesses. AXT and IVM consume it with their own exact statement and current-authority checks. State history, proof limits and transaction-validity timing come from committed protocol state. Local cache size, serving retention, wall-clock timeout, acceleration choice and available RAM never change the accepted effect or certified root. Local inability to execute defers; malformed transaction evidence rejects deterministically.
requirements.summary: Complete authenticated State and deterministic effects independent of local resources
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: **First-release identities.** Use semantic relation/parameter identities and canonical Norito frames, not source-file hashes, current executable digests or a global catalog membership hash as transaction truth. Build/source hashes remain evidence metadata. Keep a discoverable protocol inventory without coupling the availability or validity of one protocol to completion of the others. AccountId is domainless; aliases and ownership are separate State. IVM is the sole VM and ABI V1. Every build contains the required opcode/syscall/verifier semantics; hardware acceleration may have an equivalent scalar fallback.
requirements.summary: Semantic identities, canonical Norito, independent protocols, domainless accounts and unconditional ABI V1
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: **Keys and privacy.** Derive verification inputs from authoritative policies; reject unbound keys and cross-role proofs. Keep secure randomness and clearing witness/key owners, bounded canonical decoding and no private witnesses in telemetry. Separate encryption confidentiality, hidden-program privacy, proof zero knowledge, output authorization and authenticated opening; evidence for one does not establish the others. Hardware-dependent guarantees are not relabeled as software guarantees.
requirements.summary: Authoritative keys, secrecy, bounded decoding and distinct privacy guarantees
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: **Default interface.** A configured client supplies network/account/signing and local private-material custody once. Each protocol exposes typed operations such as transfer, present, prove-and-apply, evaluate or open. One asynchronous call owns parameter/context lookup, bounded resource planning, witness acquisition, encryption/proving, local verification, instruction construction, signing, submission and confirmation. SDKs supply sensible canonical defaults; normal callers choose business inputs and intended effects, not transcript layouts, proof engines, ring sizes, dummy witnesses, VK blobs or a list of intermediate RPCs. Missing ownership, issuer material or committee participation gets an actionable typed error or recoverable pending operation; no authority or key is silently fabricated.
requirements.summary: Configured one-call operation with resource planning, private custody and typed recovery
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: **Native execution.** Each final ledger operation is an ordinary serializable ISI, usable in instruction batches and through the sole IVM/Kotodama instruction path. The instruction binds its complete statement, relation, policy/key generation, account/context, expiry, replay domain and expected effect. Its Core handler performs genuine verification and applies the authorized effect atomically within that transaction, including its nullifier/nonce and resource accounting. A prior generic `VerifyProof` result is not a reusable authorization token. Effect instructions do not require a separate verification transaction; shared preverification caches are valid only for the exact authenticated proof/context and cannot skip current-State checks. A verify-only primitive returns/records verification for its typed statement without inventing a financial effect.
requirements.summary: Canonical atomic effect ISIs, contract authority, current-State checks and exact-context preverification
requirements.rationale: Supply the missing ABI V1 bridge, authority, signed declaration and large-payload/resource work explicitly; do not assume the current bridge is general.

requirements.original_text: **Private work.** Witnesses, secret keys, hidden programs and plaintext credentials stay in their authorized local/client/evaluator owners. ISIs carry only the public statement, proof, allowed ciphertexts and authenticated references. Validators execute bounded deterministic handlers and never wait for a prover, committee or external RPC. Proving and threshold share collection may take time: the single SDK invocation can await them or return a durable operation handle with typed progress, cancellation and read-only recovery. Retries reconcile the original transaction/operation and cannot apply effects twice. A timeout after submission is an unknown/pending outcome until readback establishes success or failure. Cross-lane AXT and issuer/committee protocols retain their real stages and finality; a single API call does not pretend they are one consensus round.
requirements.summary: Private work stays off-chain; durable asynchronous progress and nonduplicating recovery
requirements.rationale: Retained in full as development scope and acceptance obligations of the mapped tasks; this planning record claims no implementation, test or deployment completion.

requirements.original_text: The BFV tags are refused because the retained exact-lift encryption exposes a noiseless public-key equation; this is an identified confidentiality defect, not merely missing certification. `require_production_support` rejects both tags. Signed receipt branches and Torii signers still exist; opening and phone canonicality currently rely on signatures. SDK HTTP adapters exist, but Swift and Kotlin input-encryption helpers explicitly fail. Removing refusals alone would expose an insecure and proof-less product.

Implement a runnable costing harness that lowers every tape instruction and records ciphertext/key bytes, live buffers, noise/level bounds and proof work. Compare the existing F257 sparse-slot candidate against a measured alternative representation or batching modulus; include scalar-subalgebra input proofs, masking and broadcast/key-switch costs, unused-output zeroing and the full equality operation. Recompute encoding and automorphisms for the chosen ring instead of copying illustrative constants. Use pinned independent arithmetic fixtures and reference decryption comparisons. This selects a concrete engineering starting point, not a secure parameter profile. Derive the profile, refresh schedule and circuit-privacy constants from that complete workload and its threat model; the audit's rough dimensions, flooding estimates and proposed client-proof deferral are not adopted requirements. R.2 still includes client well-formedness proofs from the first usable slice.

### R6-0 [facts-1-2] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:37 ('usable ... through the sole IVM/Kotodama instruction path'), :62 (smart-contract composition); graph S.2

**Problem.** The plan assumes IVM already has a general way to issue ISIs. It does not. The only generic instruction syscall is a closed allow-list whose single accepted instruction always fails. Making the new privacy, credential, RAM-LFE, FHE and proved-invocation ISIs callable from Kotodama means changing the ABI V1 surface. Neither §2 nor any graph node (S.2, I.3, R.3, ...) carries that work or the ABI golden and hash updates AGENTS requires.

**Evidence.** - SYSCALL_SMARTCONTRACT_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION (0xA0) takes an operation tag. Only tag 1 = SubmitBallot (and a stale tag 2) is defined (crates/ivm_abi/src/syscalls.rs:365-368).
- The Core host rejects every other instruction with PermissionDenied (crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/ivm/host.rs:10721-10759). The docs agree: 'other instruction types are rejected' (crates/ivm/docs/syscalls.md:87).
- SubmitBallot itself always fails through ensure_qualified_standalone_zk_relation_v1 (crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/isi/world.rs:1363-1374, 14774).
- ivm_abi has no privacy, identifier, RAM-LFE, FHE-job or credential syscalls; the only SoraCloud syscalls are state and mailbox calls 0xC0-0xC9 (syscalls.rs:439-451).

**Fix.** 1. Add an IVM composition artifact to S.2 (plan §2 "Native execution", graph S.2). Pick one typed exposure mechanism that fits Kotodama's ban on raw `execute_instruction` (kotodama_surface builtins.rs:3076-3082): either typed syscalls per ISI or typed 0xA0 operation tags, each with a matching typed Kotodama builtin.
2. In the same artifact, define the authority semantics for contract-issued proof ISIs: which account or context the proof and replay domain bind to when the contract or caller lineage is the authority rather than the signer.
3. Remove the stale tag 2 (host.rs:10757 TODO). Replace or close the always-failing SubmitBallot tag as part of W.ZV.
4. Make every delivery that adds to the ABI meet the AGENTS ABI-evolution obligations: abi_syscall_list order, the abi_syscall_list_golden and abi_hash_versions goldens, pointer_type_ids_golden for any new pointer type, regenerated abi_hash with manifest positive and negative admission tests, Kotodama builtin and compiler tests, and crates/ivm/docs/syscalls.md.
5. State in §2 "Testnet history, restart and incompatible changes" that an abi_hash change follows the plan's incompatible-change rule (fresh-genesis cutover or contract redeploy). Alternatively, batch the surface additions per cutover.
6. Add an IVM/Kotodama composition test to the acceptance lists (plan:64 and plan:282) for every usable delivery. Plan:11 already requires ABI V1 artifact regeneration in general, so cite it rather than duplicating it.

### R6-2 [facts-3] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:82 (§3 Current implementation), :117 (R.3), :145-152 (source anchors); ZK plan r6 review reconciliation.md:127-128

**Problem.** The current-code inventory leaves out the third RAM-LFE backend, `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1`. It is the only backend that `require_production_support` accepts, and Core lets anyone register and activate it. Torii evaluates it on plaintext input, yet every consumer then rejects it, so it is accepted but does nothing. Neither §3 nor R.3 retires it or its wire tags. The reconciliation still marks F77/F78 as 'Carried forward', although their triage requirements explicitly ask for 'HKDF no-effect acceptance' to be listed in the inventory and for the plan to 'Remove the no-effect backend and update its consumers'. The r6 plan contains no HKDF text at all, so that carry-forward claim is false. Read as written, the inventory ('The BFV tags are refused … rejects both tags') suggests nothing else is live.

**Evidence.** crates/iroha_crypto/src/ram_lfe.rs:338-360: `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1 => Ok(())` while both BFV tags are refused. :951-990 `evaluate_hkdf_prf` returns `output: request.normalized_input.clone()` (:986), i.e. plaintext. Core accepts it: isi/ram_lfe.rs:170 `RamLfeBackend::HkdfSha3_512PrfV1 => {}`. Consumers reject it: identifier.rs:567-591 ('unsupported backend … for identifier claims'), isi/ram_lfe.rs:277-296 (stateless receipt), Torii identifier_resolution.rs:208-211 and 572-574. Wire tags appear in kotlin/core-jvm/.../RamLfeWireTags.kt, javascript/iroha_js/src/toriiClient.js, python/iroha_torii_client/identifier_receipts.py, csharp/.../IdentifierReceiptJsonConverters.cs, crates/connect_norito_bridge/src/lib.rs:3021 and crates/iroha_data_model/src/identifier.rs:1116. Running grep for 'hkdf' on the plan returns nothing. The triage JSON entries for F77/F78 hold the r6_requirement text quoted above.

**Fix.** Treat this as a minor documentation/traceability fix; no new design rule is needed.

(1) Plan §3 'Current implementation' (after plan:82): add one sentence. `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1` passes `require_production_support` (crates/iroha_crypto/src/ram_lfe.rs:356-360), and Core registers and activates self-owned HKDF policies (crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/isi/ram_lfe.rs:170; executor_initial_permission_authority.rs:1543-1545). The backend has no effect, because every consumer rejects it:
- Torii `execute_encrypted` (crates/iroha_torii/src/identifier_resolution.rs:173-177);
- identifier claims (crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/isi/identifier.rs:576-588);
- stateless receipts (isi/ram_lfe.rs:285-296).
Do not claim that Torii evaluates HKDF input.

(2) In R.3, or the plan:143 deletion sentence: state that the V1 policy schema from R.0 replaces `RamLfeBackend`. List as deleted with no alias:
- `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1`, `policy_commitment` and `evaluate_hkdf_prf`;
- the Core and Torii match arms;
- the `hkdf-sha3-512-prf-v1` tag in the bridge (crates/connect_norito_bridge/src/lib.rs:3021), the data model (crates/iroha_data_model/src/identifier.rs:1116), tools/kotlin-fixture-gen, and the Swift, Kotlin, Java-consumer, JavaScript, Python and C# SDK sources, tests and fixtures.

(3) Add both anchors to the §3 source-anchor list (plan:145-152).

(4) Reconciliation rows F77/F78 (reconciliation:127-128): leave them as 'Carried forward' only once (1)-(3) exist, and cite the new plan sentences.

### R6-3 [facts-4-5] dist/reports/ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:24, :120, :163, :240, :253-255 (with graph D.0 / W.ZA)

**Problem.** ZK-AMS already contains a second, complete multi-key RLWE homomorphic-encryption stack (MKHE). It has its own RNS moduli and negacyclic arithmetic, relinearization and Galois keys, collective (threshold) key generation, collective key switching (CKS) and machine-checked noise certificates. The plan says nothing about it. §2 calls for 'one exact modular RNS owner shared by RAM-LFE and SoraCloud'. R.1 builds a new RNS-BGV stack and R.6 builds new threshold key generation and decryption shares. §5 deletes 'duplicate FHE drivers'. The W7 ZK-AMS row names only 'phases II/III' (the MKHE phase23 code) and a PCS choice. The only MKHE mention anywhere is its proof-hash digest (:163). Binding direction 2 requires one implementation per semantic role and the deletion of duplicate drivers, so the plan as written would add a third FHE implementation with no reuse-or-distinct decision. The D.0 deletion inventory cannot be complete or checkable without one.

**Evidence.** crates/iroha_zkp_halo2/src/vega/zk_ams/mkhe.rs:1105-1126 (own RNS `moduli` and `negacyclic_roots` tables), :2680 (`fn relinearize`); mkhe/collective_keys.rs:1-6 (one compact relinearization key plus 31 Galois keys, collective evaluated keys); mkhe/cks.rs:1 (collective key switching); mkhe/noise.rs:1-20 (noise certificate covering ring_degree, party_count and RNS/hybrid limbs); mkhe/resource.rs:98 (rosters of 2..=8 parties). No iroha_crypto::fhe_bfv import exists under crates/iroha_zkp_halo2/src/vega/zk_ams. Plan :163 is the only MKHE reference; plan :240 does not relate ZK-AMS phases II/III to the shared FHE owner.

**Fix.** 1. In §2 FHE (plan:24) and §5 (plan:255), add ZK-AMS MKHE to an explicit FHE inventory. Name its location (crates/iroha_zkp_halo2/src/vega/zk_ams/mkhe*). Describe it accurately: a multi-key RNS-BGV with T256 plaintext and a 2..=8 party roster, Halo2/Bulletproof-proven collective keys and decryption shares, test-only ring/NTT/relinearization/Galois/CKS reference code, and a fail-closed production surface.

2. Record a decision with a rationale. Either:
   (a) Treat the multi-key collective protocol, its proofs and wire as a distinct semantic role. When W.ZA makes phases II/III usable, ZK-AMS takes its production RNS/NTT/key-switch arithmetic from the shared R.1 owner. Add R.1 to W.ZA's `requires`, and list MKHE's test-only arithmetic core as superseded in D.0.
   (b) Or exclude it explicitly from "duplicate FHE drivers" and from the shared owner, with the concrete reason, for example an incompatible ring degree or plaintext modulus that one owner cannot serve.

3. In R.1 and R.6, cite MKHE as the design reference, consistent with the audit's verdict: profile validation, limb-major layout, CBD/rejection sampling, security-certificate digest, resource ceilings, collective key generation and the smudged decryption-share/CKS structure. Do not leave this reuse implicit through an archived report.

4. Make D.0's FHE deletion list checkable by enumerating these explicitly: fhe_bfv including eight_party_decryption, the generic binding-only routes, and the MKHE disposition chosen above.

### R6-5 [facts-4-5] dist/reports/ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:220 (W5 freshness formula)

**Problem.** The deadline formula uses 'latest certificate expiry Cmax'. The relation requires the presentation window end to lie within every certificate in the presented path. The binding bound is therefore the earliest not_after (the minimum over the chain), not the latest. With 'latest', any chain whose CA certificate expires before the leaf yields a budgeted deadline after the proof becomes unprovable. Holders and CA-cadence budgets derived from this formula would plan against a deadline the relation rejects.

**Evidence.** crates/iroha_core_privacy/src/privacy_engines/zk_x509/der_air.rs:4151-4156 (each certificate requires presentation_not_after <= certificate.not_after); :4034-4060 and :4086 (per-row `before_not_after` range-witness constraints); crates/iroha_core_privacy/src/privacy_state.rs:2386-2402 (block second <= PA, PA < NU, PA - TU <= 300).

**Fix.** In dist/reports/ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:220, replace "latest certificate expiry Cmax" with "earliest not_after Cmin over every certificate in the presented path (leaf, intermediate and root)". Write the deadline as `min(TU+301, NU, Cmin+1, PA+1)*1000-1`. Cite the per-certificate check at relation.rs:276-281 and der_air.rs:4151-4156 / :4086. Add required tests: a chain whose intermediate (and, separately, root) certificate expires before the leaf. Each test must show that a block second of Cmin is accepted, Cmin+1 is rejected, and the holder's budgeted deadline matches Cmin.

findings.summary: The deadline formula uses 'latest certificate expiry Cmax'. The relation requires the presentation window end to lie within every certificate in the presented path. The binding bound is therefore the earliest not_after (the minimum over the chain), not the latest. With 'latest', any chain whose CA certificate expires before the leaf yields a budgeted deadline after the proof becomes unprovable. Holders and CA-cadence budgets derived from this formula would plan against a deadline the relation rejects.
findings.rationale: Use the earliest certificate expiry across the chain; keep certificate inclusivity, CRL nextUpdate exclusion and overflow/boundary tests exact.

**Problem.** The plan selects the WG tree/hash after in-circuit witness measurements on the W1 AIR interface. In the graph, G.0 'Complete keyed State root, table coverage and canonical result layout' is a root. The measurement task G.3 depends on G.1, which depends on G.0, so the plan's selection order cannot be expressed without a cycle. Section 6 also puts full table/publication coverage after the first usable result, while the usable G.2 requires G.0's 'complete table coverage'.

**Evidence.** Plan:183 says 'Select the tree/hash using native benchmarks and actual in-circuit witness measurements after W1 exposes the AIR interface'. Plan:266 lists 'Measured in-circuit witnesses and full table/publication coverage' under 'Continue to full outcome'. The JSON gives G.0 requires [] and G.3 requires [G.1, F.0]. checker:205-207 enforces that G.2 has no F.* ancestor, i.e. it ships before any in-circuit measurement exists.

**Fix.** Make the WG selection order expressible without a cycle.
1. Split G.0:
   - G.0a, a root node: complete table/root inventory, native keyed-tree prototype and native benchmarks.
   - G.0b: final authoritative tree/hash, complete table/publication coverage and the E51 amendment. G.0b requires G.3 and G.0a.
2. Rebase G.1 and G.3 on G.0a.
3. Say explicitly which root G.2 ships on:

State in the WG section that replacing it with G.0b on a testnet already in use requires an explicit fresh genesis, since no old-layout replay code is kept (plan:185). Add a usable WG step after G.0b, or make G.2 require G.0b for its full outcome.
   - Option (b): drop "after W1 exposes the AIR interface" from plan:183, fix the tree/hash in G.0 from native benchmarks plus labeled projections, and limit G.3 to confirming them. A disagreement then becomes fresh-genesis replacement work.
4. Make A.0 and I.1, whose in-circuit WG witnesses must target the final tree, require G.0b instead of just G.1/G.3.
5. Align the Section 6 Authenticated State row (plan:266) with the graph: "full table/publication coverage" must sit in the same column as the node that delivers it.
6. Add a checker assertion that the final-root node has a G.3 ancestor while G.2 still has no F.* ancestor through the prototype path.

**Problem.** The live `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1` backend is accepted as 'production supported' and evaluates a plaintext keyed PRF held by the resolver. That is a trusted-resolver, OPRF-style substitute running in parallel with the planned FHE path. The 'Current implementation' paragraph omits it, and no task retires it. This conflicts with direction 3 ('not ... an OPRF-only substitute') and direction 2 (one implementation per semantic role). The reconciliation nevertheless marks F77/F78 (HKDF inventory and retirement) as 'Carried forward', which it defines as 'has a place in the current plan'.

**Fix.** Change the severity to minor and fix the wording. HKDF is a no-effect tag: it can be registered and activated in Signed mode, but Torii never evaluates it, and identifier claims and stateless receipts reject it. Do not call it a parallel substitute.

1. Current implementation (plan:82): add one sentence. `require_production_support` accepts `HkdfSha3_512PrfV1` (ram_lfe.rs:358), so Signed HKDF policies register and activate with no effect. 2. Source anchors (plan:147): relabel 356–361 as "BFV refusal, HKDF acceptance". Add 631–639 (HKDF builder) and 951–990 (HKDF evaluator).
3. R.3 (plan:117): name the deletion explicitly, alongside removing Signed mode. Remove the HKDF backend tag together with its evaluator, its builder and the Core registration arm. In the same change, regenerate its Torii, data-model, Rust/Swift/Kotlin/JS/Java/C#/Python consumers and fixtures, so that `RegisterRamLfeProgramPolicy` admits only the canonical class-bound V1 policy.
4. Add negative tests (plan:136): the removed HKDF tag is rejected at Norito and JSON decoding and at registration, including when it is combined with Proof mode once the verifier lands.

### R6-13 [direction] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:96, :117 (R.3), :131

**Problem.** The plan states that 'Phone ownership authentication is a separate permission/attestation question' but assigns it to no task. Meanwhile R.3 removes the signature-based phone path and makes ClaimIdentifier, followed by lookup, usable immediately. Accounts may claim for themselves, so after R.3 nothing in the plan stops any account from binding any well-formed phone number to itself. Payments addressed to that phone number would then route to the squatter. This unsafe consequence is not handled.

**Evidence.** crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/isi/identifier.rs:397 (`authority == account` authorizes a self-claim); :432-438 and :769-773 (current phone#retail requires a pinned attestor key); :450-458 (and a Signed programmed policy, which R.3 removes). Plan :131 'Account/alias permissions are tested separately' gives no owner.

**Fix.** Give the task to R.0, which specifies it, and to R.3, which implements it before phone claims become usable. Also list it under "Explicitly unresolved" (:140) while the construction is still open.

1. Define one canonical phone#retail claim-authorization statement. It binds network, policy, nullifier, beneficiary account/UAID, expiry and replay domain. It is checked inside ClaimIdentifier against a verifier commitment named in the authoritative policy. Either:
   - (a) an ownership attestation from the policy's registered verifier, or a proof of one; or
   - (b) a rule that only the policy owner or a registrar account it authorizes may submit phone claims. In that case, change ensure_policy_authorized (identifier.rs:397) so that self-claims are rejected for phone#retail, and say so in R.3.
2. State that this check does not replace the execution, opening or nullifier-derivation proofs (:96).
3. Define dispute and re-binding through RevokeIdentifier.
4. In the acceptance tests (:131-135), add:
   - a squat of someone else's number;
   - a race between two first claims;
   - a hijack attempt on an existing binding;
   - a statement replayed or reused for a different beneficiary;
   - a revoked or rotated verifier.

**Problem.** SoraCloud bootstrap/threshold delivery (C.2) requires the RAM-LFE usable deliveries R.5 and R.6, including RAM-LFE-specific tape proofs and Torii/SDK work. C.0 transitively requires R.0, the RAM-LFE threat model and policy schema, via R.1. **Fix.** Split shared FHE artifacts out of the RAM-LFE deliveries in zk-plan-r6-graph.json and the plan's R table (:112-121), then regenerate the graph:

1. **Split R.1.** Add a new implementation node, e.g. `R.1a`/`H.0`, for the shared exact modular RNS-BGV owner from :24/:123: arithmetic, NTT/basis conversion, keygen/enc/dec, relinearization, modulus switching, automorphisms, codecs, randomness and clearing. It requires only S.0. R.1 keeps the RAM-LFE full-tape cost harness and RAM-LFE profile derivation, and requires R.0 plus the shared node. C.0 then requires the shared node instead of R.1.

3. **Add a shared threshold node.** It covers threshold keygen/custody, verifiable decryption-share proofs, bounded combining and key epochs. It requires the shared RNS node and F.1. R.6 then requires R.3 plus this node and keeps only the integration with the RAM-LFE opening statement and the retirement of the single authority.

4. **Rewire C.2** to require C.1, the bootstrapping node, the threshold node and S.2. Drop R.5 and R.6. SoraCloud keeps its own full-bootstrap job and threshold-request statements (:251, :253).

5. **Update plan §5 :255** to say that SoraCloud bootstrap/threshold delivery consumes the shared FHE bootstrapping and threshold primitives, not the RAM-LFE deliveries.

6. **Add a check-script assertion** that no C.* node has R.2, R.3, R.4, R.5 or R.6 as an ancestor. This mirrors check.py:67 and extends check.py:209-211 to C.2.

### R6-18 [isi-sdk] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:37, :62, :64; zk-plan-r6-graph.json (no composition node)

**Problem.** The plan says every ISI is usable 'through the sole IVM/Kotodama instruction path' and that the prepared form supports 'smart-contract composition'. No such general path exists. Under ABI V1 memory limits the requirement cannot be met for heavy operations, and no task or acceptance test covers it.

**Evidence.** - The Core IVM bridge for SMARTCONTRACT_EXECUTE_INSTRUCTION accepts only tag SUBMIT_BALLOT; every other tag returns PermissionDenied (crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/ivm/host.rs:10720-10759). The ABI labels the bridge 'development API' (crates/ivm_abi/src/syscalls.rs:364-370). Kotodama's VendorInstructionKind has only SubmitBallot (crates/kotodama_lang/src/compiler.rs:5299-5306).
- The bridge decodes the whole InstructionBox from VM memory (host.rs:8920-8923). VM memory is a 1 MiB heap (HEAP_START 0x100000 to INPUT_START 0x200000) and a 64 KiB INPUT region (crates/ivm/src/memory.rs:303-315). Contract argument records are capped at 1 MiB (crates/iroha_data_model/src/transaction/executable.rs:147). So no contract can carry an X509 presentation, whose proof cap of 9,437,184 bytes the plan keeps (plan:216), nor any proof or ciphertext over about 1 MiB.
- Contract-emitted instructions are queued and applied only after the VM finishes (host.rs:2693-2727). A contract therefore never sees the 'actual result', such as an opened identifier.
- The acceptance tests (plan:64) cover only direct ISI and prepared/batched use. No graph node owns new ABI V1 tags/syscalls, Kotodama builtins or abi_hash/golden regeneration, all of which AGENTS.md requires.

**Fix.** 1. In plan §developer-isi (plan:37, :62), replace "the sole IVM/Kotodama instruction path" with a precise contract that S.2 owns. It should name one route: either typed operation tags or syscalls per ISI on the ABI V1 instruction bridge (0xA0 today, which accepts only SubmitBallot, host.rs:10720-10759), or one typed generic bridge. Also remove the "development API" status of that bridge (syscalls.rs:364) and its unused declared tags.
2. Define how proofs, ciphertexts and witness references larger than the V1 limits reach a contract. Options are by-reference access to signed-transaction ProofAttachments (signed.rs:286-292) through a typed syscall, or an explicit change to the V1 memory map (memory.rs:303-315) and to MAX_CONTRACT_ARGUMENT_RECORD_BYTES (executable.rs:147). Otherwise, state explicitly which operations (for example X509 presentations up to 9,437,184 bytes) are composable only through the prepared/batched transaction route.
3. State the effect semantics. Contract-emitted ISIs are queued and applied after the VM finishes (host.rs:8938-8950, 2635-2727). Their results, such as an opened identifier, are therefore not visible within the same invocation and must be read in a later invocation.
4. Add a graph node, or extend S.2's title and acceptance, for the ABI V1 surface. It should cover new tags or syscalls, Kotodama builtins (VendorInstructionKind at compiler.rs:5299), abi_syscall_list, abi_hash, the golden tests (abi_syscall_list_golden.rs, abi_hash_versions.rs) and crates/ivm/docs/syscalls.md. Make the W3 syscall coverage (I.0) include the new entries.
5. Add a Kotodama-composition four-validator test for each composable operation to plan:64 and plan:282, and to developer_surface_contract (graph:910).

### R6-19 [isi-sdk] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:216, :222, :64; delivery graph X.2

**Problem.** The plan keeps the 9,437,184-byte X509 proof cap and requires maximum-proof submissions and four-validator effect tests. It never addresses the committed consensus block payload limit, which is smaller than one such transaction. The maximum X509 flow cannot be committed under the default chain parameters.

**Evidence.** - The default max_block_bytes is 4 MiB (crates/iroha_data_model/src/parameter/system.rs:1491-1494).
- The Sumeragi header rule is payload_len ≤ max_block_bytes(h) (specs/sumeragi.md:261, :1082), with 4 MiB in the §9.3 table (specs/sumeragi.md:2296).
- The default max_tx_bytes is 10 MiB (system.rs:1568-1571). The privacy limits allow 9 MiB per action and 18 MiB per block (crates/iroha_data_model/src/privacy/tests/protocol_and_proofs.rs:2304-2307), which is inconsistent with the 4 MiB block payload.
- Raising max_block_bytes is constrained by sync_max_bytes, transport frame and DA payload checks (crates/iroha_sumeragi/src/pacemaker.rs:138-182).
- I found no genesis or config override.

**Fix.** In W5 (and the shared resource rules in §2/§6), add a requirement that the canonical testnet genesis sets limits a maximum-shape privacy transaction can actually fit in:
- `max_block_bytes` ≥ the largest admitted privacy transaction's encoded length + `PAYLOAD_OVERHEAD`, while staying within the transport cap (17 MiB − 64 KiB `FRAME_OVERHEAD`) and the epoch DA `max_payload_size_bytes`.
- `sync_max_bytes` ≥ `max_block_bytes` + 64 KiB.
- `max_tx_bytes` ≥ that transaction's encoded length.

Make the privacy limits consistent with these parameters, and enforce that at parameter validation:
- per-block privacy bytes ≤ `max_block_bytes` (currently 18 MiB vs 4 MiB);
- per-action and per-transaction privacy bytes ≤ min(`max_tx_bytes`, `max_block_bytes` − overhead).

Account for block propagation and verification time against `e_max`/`a_max` and the 1-second cadence. Reject at admission any transaction that can never fit in a block, with a typed error, instead of letting it wait until it expires.

Add acceptance tests:
- a maximum-proof X509 transaction, and a PQ-MASP one, is actually included, committed and replayed on four validators;
- a negative test showing an oversized transaction is rejected at admission rather than left in the queue.

Add the parameter/genesis change as an explicit dependency of X.2 and of the maximum-shape W7 nodes in the graph JSON.

### R6-21 [critic] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:96, :117, :131

**Problem.** The plan itself says phone ownership authentication is 'a separate permission/attestation question', but no task, owner or acceptance test covers it. R.3 still ships ClaimIdentifier for identifiers as immediately usable. In current code, any account can self-claim, and the canonical keyed nullifier makes the first claim to a given phone number exclusive. So once R.3 lands, anyone who knows a victim's number can permanently bind it to their own account. The documented resolve -> transfer flow would then send the victim's incoming payments to the squatter. Today the canonicality attestor signature at least gives a point where control could be checked; the plan removes it (:96) and puts nothing in its place.

**Evidence.** identifier.rs:392-399: authority == account is enough to claim. specs/universal_accounts_guide.md:66-73: the nullifier means 'a second ciphertext for the same phone cannot bind another UAID', and resolution is resolve -> transfer. The graph (zk-plan-r6-graph.json) has no ownership task; R.0 and R.3 titles cover threat model and claim but not ownership. Plan:131 says 'Account/alias permissions are tested separately'.

**Fix.** Make phone-number control an explicit requirement owned by R.0, R.2 and R.3, and add it to the graph's R.0/R.3 titles or contracts.

- R.0: the threat model covers squatting on a victim's number and states what counts as authorized control of a number.
- R.2/R.3: `ClaimIdentifier` for `phone#retail` accepts one of two forms of control evidence alongside the canonicality/nullifier proof:
  - (a) A policy-pinned control attestation bound to network, policy, nullifier, beneficiary UAID/AccountId and expiry. This is an ordinary permission, not a substitute for the derivation proof, so it is consistent with :96.
  - (b) Opener-side authorization of phone queries, bound to the same tuple.
- Acceptance tests (R.3/R.7):
  - Claiming a victim's number fails without control evidence.
  - Replaying control evidence for a different beneficiary or nullifier fails.
  - Policy-owner revocation and expiry give the real holder the number back.
- Until control evidence is implemented, `phone#retail ClaimIdentifier` returns the typed unsupported-operation error from :15. Non-phone identifier policies are not blocked.
- Drop the word 'permanently' from the impact statement: policy-owner revocation and expiry already exist as correction paths.

### R6-22 [critic] ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:231 vs :232-241, :71

**Problem.** Per-pool turnstile and supply caps are required only for Orchard. Relations go live without waiting for review, which is non-blocking (:141, :271). For PQ-MASP, atomic settlement, FCMP++ and confidential assets, an underconstrained relation could mint shielded value that then exits into transparent assets with no deterministic bound. Public reserve custody exists today only for Orchard and IVM private notes; PGC has its own total-supply pool invariant. A turnstile is a deterministic transaction rule, not an activation gate.

**Evidence.** crates/iroha_core_privacy/src/privacy_state.rs:4535-4538: PRIVACY_PUBLIC_RESERVE_PROTOCOLS_V1 = [Orchard, IvmPrivateNote]. PGC total_supply is used at crates/iroha_core/src/smartcontracts/isi/privacy.rs:4635. Plan:232, :233 and :241 require conservation but no reserve or turnstile accounting.

**Fix.** 1. Put one deterministic rule in the shared W7 paragraph (:245), mirror it in the :44 ISI table, and extend :71: every value-bearing shielded pool with a transparent boundary keeps a per-pool, per-asset public reserve in committed State. That covers Orchard, IVM private notes, PQ-MASP, atomic settlement, FCMP++ and confidential assets. Shields deposit into the reserve and unshields or settlement exits withdraw from it, so cumulative exits can never exceed deposits plus any backed bootstrap amount. Generalize the existing reserve-custody owner (privacy_state.rs:4535 PRIVACY_PUBLIC_RESERVE_PROTOCOLS_V1, and execute_verified_privacy_pool_public_balance_transfer) instead of adding a second mechanism.
2. Any shielded value seeded at genesis or bootstrap, such as PQ-MASP initial_note_commitments, must be matched by an equal reserve deposit when the pool is admitted. Optional per-pool supply caps are likewise State rules.
3. Fixed-supply closed pools such as PGC keep their total-supply invariant and say explicitly that they have no transparent exit.
4. Add these to every value-bearing W.* acceptance list (W.OR, W.NF, W.FC, W.CV): a test that a deliberately inflated shielded balance, from a mutated or test-only relation witness, cannot withdraw beyond the reserve; over-cap shield rejection; reserve exclusivity across pools; reserve state preserved across cold restart and full replay; and four-validator effects.
5. Mention the supply control in the graph titles for W.NF, W.FC and W.CV, as W.OR already does.
6. Record in the reconciliation that this restores r5's W7.T scope for the note family.

findings.summary: Per-pool turnstile and supply caps are required only for Orchard. Relations go live without waiting for review, which is non-blocking (:141, :271). For PQ-MASP, atomic settlement, FCMP++ and confidential assets, an underconstrained relation could mint shielded value that then exits into transparent assets with no deterministic bound. Public reserve custody exists today only for Orchard and IVM private notes; PGC has its own total-supply pool invariant. A turnstile is a deterministic transaction rule, not an activation gate.
findings.rationale: Add independently enforced per-pool/per-asset reserves or the applicable fixed-supply invariant, with funded bootstrap, exclusivity and restart tests. Bound residual economic exposure without calling reserves proof soundness.

### F2 [issues-0-10] Plan §13 Activation bullet, /Users/takemiyamakoto/devstuff/iroha/dist/reports/ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:1825-1829

**Problem.** Issue #1 is unresolved in §13. #1's fix explicitly named §13 and required the old "qualification digest" wording to be replaced by authorization through a qualification record signed by the release-pinned qualification-signer key set. Revision 5's §13 still says activation means "a governed protocol-state transition installs the qualified digest". It does not mention the signed record, the pinned signers, or that governance can only tighten. The adopted objective therefore still describes activation as a governance-only procedure, which is the property #1 found missing. W0.D2's summary of the adopted text, items (a) to (j), also leaves out activation authority.

**Fix.** In plan §13 (Executable objective):
(1) Replace the Activation bullet (plan:1826-1827) with: "**Activation:** on a production-class network, a governed protocol-state transition installs a qualification record signed by a threshold of the release-pinned qualification-signer key set (W6.REL.K, verified by W6.G). The record binds the chain id and genesis hash, the capability scope, the compiled capability digest, and the snapshot and binary digests, and it is never node config, an environment variable or a Cargo feature. Governance alone (CanEnactGovernance) can only tighten: suspend, retire, or install a one-way refusal. Resuming needs a newer signed record. ### F3 [issues-0-10] Graph W0.9 (/Users/takemiyamakoto/devstuff/iroha/dist/reports/ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md:287); plan §0 Networks and releases (/Users/takemiyamakoto/devstuff/

**Problem.** W0.9 cannot meet its own criterion before W6.P exists.

- **The criterion.** W0.9 closes only when the refusal is in force on Minamoto, "on a release shown to replay Minamoto's certified blocks and reproduce every certified R, a patch on its deployed release line if needed".
- **The release model.** It says every production-class deployment is a W6.P-signed candidate. Tightening releases appear only as a sub-case of that rule (A10). The history-replay check is W6.P check (2).
- **The graph.** W0.9 depends only on W6.REL.D and W0.D1.W0, and W6.P is not among its ancestors. W6.P itself depends on W0.3, W0.2, W6.H and W0.D5.
- **The conflict.** Either W0.9 waits for W6.P, which undercuts "W0.9 refuses ... now" in the Summary and §0, or the plan must exempt tightening patches from W6.P signing and define who certifies the replay. Neither is stated, and "a patch on its deployed release line" contradicts "Every production-class deployment is a W6.P-signed candidate".

**Fix.** Pick one option and record it in plan §0, graph A10 (:184-187), W6.REL.D item (3) (:504) and W0.9's criterion (:287).

(A) Explicit tightening exemption (keeps "now"). Add to A10 and W6.REL.D item (3) a rule along these lines:

"A tightening-only release adds no capability code and no Proposed-state entry; it only refuses or fixes. Before W6.P closes, such a release may be deployed without W6.P signing. It is then signed by the W6.REL.D accountable operator role. It carries a source digest, per-platform binary digests, the focused tests of the tightening milestone and, for each network that keeps its history, a read-only replay of that network's certified blocks that reproduces every certified R. The tightening milestone performs that replay and records it. After W6.P closes, tightening releases are W6.P-signed like any other release."

Then reword W0.9's criterion to name this path for both Taira and Minamoto. Name the signer, and name the W0.9-owned Minamoto replay export and its result. Also remove the contradiction between "a patch on its deployed release line" and "Every production-class deployment is a W6.P-signed candidate".

(B) Split W0.9. W0.9 itself covers the code, the tests and the genesis refusal height on integration networks and kagami profiles, and depends on W6.REL.D and W0.D1.W0. A new W0.9.DEP covers the in-force refusal on Taira and Minamoto: the Taira reset genesis or governed transition, plus the Minamoto governed transition on a release that passes W6.P check (2). W0.9.DEP depends on W0.9 and W6.P, and W6.IC depends on W0.9.DEP. The Taira leg must sit in W0.9.DEP too, because a Taira deployment is also production-class. Under this option the Summary and §0 should say that the refusal is built now and deployed at the first W6.P candidate, not that it is in force "now".

### F4 [issues-0-10] Graph W1.X3 (/Users/takemiyamakoto/devstuff/iroha/dist/reports/ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md:342)

**Problem.** The certified-history criterion that the #0 resolution added to W1.X3 cannot be met as written. After the Binding-AIR route is deleted, a node restarting "from genesis" cannot reproduce roots for transactions that the route accepted. If any exist, the W6.REL.H boundary must lie above them, and then they are not re-executed at all. The criterion also says those transactions ran "before W1.A.GEN", but from the W0.9 refusal height they were refused. The relevant height is W0.9's, and W0.9 already records the count of accepted binding-route verifications per network.

**Fix.** **W1.X3 (graph :342).** Replace the "Certified-history replay" sentence with:

> "Certified-history replay: on each production-class network that keeps its history, a node built from the deleting release restarts as follows.
> (a) If W0.9's recorded count of accepted binding-route verifications and binding-only STARK registrations on that network is zero, it restarts from genesis.
> (b) Otherwise it restarts from the network's W6.REL.H boundary, which lies above the last such accepted transaction (at or above the W0.9 refusal height suffices).
> Either way it reproduces every certified root from that start. Every transaction that W0.9 refused at or above its refusal height and that lies within the replayed range replays with the same typed rejection after the gate code is removed, since the transaction results are committed in R (specs/sumeragi.md E51)."

Delete "executed through the Binding-AIR route before W1.A.GEN". Wherever the bound is still needed, write "below the W0.9 refusal height".

**W1.X2 (:337).** Apply the same pattern: replay from genesis only if no fork-ID proof was accepted on that network before W1.A.RACE. Otherwise replay from the W6.REL.H boundary above those proofs.

**W1.X4 (:343).** Apply the same pattern, and replace "before W4.A.SC" with "below the W0.9 refusal height". Registrations refused at or above that height must replay with the same typed rejection after stark.rs is deleted.

**Problem.** Part of issue #5 is left over, and the verifier had flagged it: W4.E2 assumes the classes are already defined.

- **What W4.E2 does.** It sizes "the RAM-LFE workload at the class maximum shape" and prices it.
- **Where the shape is fixed.** The class maximum shapes (instruction, register, state-lane and step bounds, and depth D) are fixed only at W4.D7, which depends on W4.E2. Plan §7.3 leaves these numbers to W4.D7 and calls the diagnostic profile "not a security target".
- **The consequence.** W4.D7 item (4) sets per-class budgets "at each class's maximum shape ... each citing its W4.E2 measurement". Nothing ensures W4.E2 measured the shape that W4.D7 finally chooses.

**W4.D7 item (4) (graph :409).** Add: "Each budget is stated at a shape whose bounds are no smaller than the bounds fixed in (1), and cites the W4.E2 measurement at that shape. If any bound fixed in (1) exceeds what W4.E2 measured, the record cites a new measurement at the chosen bounds, with workload, parameters and hardware, before W4.D7 closes." This relies on the fixed, padded proof shape making cost depend only on the class maximum.

**Plan §7.3 (:1056) and §7.7.** Add one line to each saying that W4.E2 records the candidate bounds it measures, and that W4.D7 budgets rest on a measurement at bounds no smaller than those finally chosen.

**Problem.** Issue #17(a) is only partly fixed. Revision 5 moves the at-most-1% unattributed-time check into each adapter's own milestone, but W4.7's completion criterion requires 'the complete W6.M phase tree with unattributed time at most 1%' while W6.M is neither a direct dependency nor an ancestor of W4.7.    W4.D.RL and W4.D.THR are acceptable alternatives for W4.5/W4.8 and W4.4 because they come after those milestones. W4.D7 is not, because it comes before W4.6a.

4. At plan:1460, change "from the W6.M evidence builder" to "from the W6.MB evidence builder, with its phase tree from W6.M instrumentation", matching the graph's W5.5 row.

### F13 [issues-22-32] Plan §8.2 cadence bullets (ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:1318-1319, 1322), 'CA-side precondition' (:1337-1341) and 'Revocation latency' (:1350); graph A7 (ZK plan 

**Problem.** Revision 5 contradicts itself on how fast a CA may issue CRLs, and the CA precondition it records is not sufficient once R_min exists. Plan :1318 says 'A CA that issues faster than R_min is acceptable.' A7 :156 and W5.A :461 instead require each CA to issue 'inside the region' [P + X, min(301, NU−TU) − d_pub,max], and plan :1319 defines that region. W5.D1(b), W5.D6's per-CA classification and plan :1337 make U_max + d_pub,max <= min(301, NU − TU) the only CA condition (the registration precondition). That condition has no lower bound on U and no R_min term. Inside the region, U >= max(R_min, P + X), so it does imply freshness and continuity. For a CA issuing faster than R_min it implies neither: the rotator publishes at most every R_min, so continuity needs R_min + d_pub,max <= min(301, NU − TU), and freshness needs d_pub,max + P + X <= min(301, NU − TU) − 0.001. The same regime also breaks the stated latency bounds. Worst-case latency <= U_max + J + d_obs + d_prep + P + L_sub (plan :1322) and W5.D6's wall-clock revocation latency <= U_max + d_pub,max both assume that published CRLs are spaced by the CA's U. Under R_min skipping, published CRLs are spaced by R_min, which is larger. So #29 (the CA precondition) and #30 (the latency claims) are resolved incorrectly for the regime the plan explicitly allows.

**Fix.** Pick one rule and apply it everywhere: plan §8.2 :1318-1322, :1337-1341, :1350 and :1370-1376, plus graph A7 :149-156, W5.D1(b) :444, W5.E1 :462, W5.D6 :465, W5.F :447, W5.I2 :459 and W5.A :461.

Preferred fix, option (b), which keeps fast CAs and matches the continuity row at :1314:

1. **Precondition.** Make the CA precondition the full per-CA envelope:
   - continuity: max(U_max, R_min) + d_pub,max ≤ min(301, NU−TU)_min for that CA;
   - freshness: d_pub,max + P + X ≤ min(301, NU−TU)_min − 0.001 for every supported platform.

   Check it at trust-anchor and CRL-lineage registration against the R_min currently in force. Make any governed transition that raises R_min check the same inequality against every active CA, and refuse the transition otherwise.
2. **W5.D6.** Classify each target CA against this full precondition before computing S and the R_min range. A failing CA is recorded as unsupported; it does not empty the range or the platform budgets. Separately, a platform with P > B, not just B ≤ 0, is unsupported.
3. **A7 and W5.A.** Replace "issues inside the region" with "meets the W5.D1 CA precondition under its recorded operator commitment".
4. **Latency.** Define the published spacing as U_pub = max(U, R_min).
   - Worst-case latency (:1322): ≤ U_pub,max + J + d_obs + d_prep + P + L_sub.
   - Revocation latency (:1350 and W5.D6): installed within max(U_max, R_min) + d_pub,max ≤ min(301, NU−TU) of the previous published thisUpdate.
5. **Tests.** Add a W5.F case and a matching W5.I2 leg. A fixture CA issuing below R_min with NU−TU < R_min + d_pub,max, or with NU−TU − 0.001 < d_pub,max + P + X, is either refused at registration or shows the gap or zero admissions. A compliant fast CA admits a proof every cycle, and its measured revocation latency stays within max(U_max, R_min) + d_pub,max.

Option (a), if fast CAs should not be allowed: delete :1318 and make the precondition max(R_min, P + X) ≤ U_min together with U_max + d_pub,max ≤ min(301, NU−TU), with the same change at registration, W5.D6 and W5.A.

### F14 [issues-22-32] Graph W5.L1 acceptance criterion (ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md:451); plan §8.1 'W5.L1 closes only when its pin grep returns nothing…' (ZK privacy and FHE plan.

**Problem.** The mechanical check that #23 asked for is broken in the Markdown appendix. The Markdown renderer replaced every '|' in the regex with '/', so the pattern is one literal string that matches nothing. The acceptance criterion therefore passes before any pin has changed. The JSON graph keeps the correct alternation, so the two artifacts disagree. Plan §8.1 cites 'its pin grep' without giving the pattern, which leaves the broken Markdown form as the only executable one agents will read. §15 item 31 claims 'every closure rg is pipe-free, one -e per alternative', which is false for this check. The check is the only catch-all for pins outside the explicit inventory, and the plan itself warns that a stale descriptor is silently wrong rather than rejected.

**Fix.** 1. In both the JSON source and the Markdown appendix, replace the W5.L1 acceptance pattern with this command: `rg -n -e '\b136\b' -e '1_?81[56]' -e '\b696\b' -e '2_?099' -e '2_?100' -e '\b157\b' -e '6_?195' -e 'q136' -e 'fri136' -e 'mask1816' -e 'mask2100' <zk_x509/> <aggregate_stark.rs> <FASTPQ X509 adapter and checker paths>`. Today it matches the same 117 lines as the intended alternation.
2. Put the same literal command in plan §8.1 in place of "its pin grep".
3. In the graph generator, make the check enforce the :356 rule at the source rather than compare '/' against '|': fail if any rg command in the JSON contains an unescaped '|' inside a pattern.
4. After regenerating, assert that every rg command in the Markdown appendix is byte-identical to the command in its JSON source.
5. Keep §15 item 31 only once these checks pass.

### F15 [issues-22-32] Plan §8.1 'What the existing analysis does not establish' (ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:1199); graph W5.RBR (ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md:448); §14 decisions tab

**Problem.** The security model, κ, Q, the absolute RBR term and the qROM gap are now stated correctly. The required owner decision on the oracle model, however, has nowhere to be recorded. Both the plan and W5.RBR say that keeping the classical-ROM model 'is recorded as an owner decision'. W5.RBR is a construction milestone, though, and no decision node records the choice: not W5.D4, not W6.D0.X509, and no row in §14. W6.D0.X509 signs the review scope before W5.RBR without naming the oracle model. Under A9 and the decision-node convention, an owner choice about the guarantee level needs its own decision record.

**Fix.** Add a decision node W5.D7, "X509 Fiat-Shamir oracle model", depending on W0.D1.W5. The owner records either:
- the classical-ROM, work-normalized BCS bound (transparent_stark.rs:159-167,710-738), with X509 labelled classical in the docs because the relation verifies P-256 ECDSA; or
- a qROM bound, which then becomes part of the W5.RBR derivation and the W6.R.X509 review.

Graph and plan changes:
- Make W5.RBR depend on W5.D7. Replace "A classical choice is recorded as an owner decision" with "targets the oracle model recorded in W5.D7".
- Make W6.D0.X509 depend on W5.D7, and have its signed scope name the model, "the W5.RBR reduction under the W5.D7 oracle model". This follows the W6.D0.OR / W7.D1 pattern. W6.R.X509 then covers that model. The graph stays acyclic, because W5.D7 depends only on W0.D1.W5.
- Add W5.D7 to the W0.D1.W5 list of W5 roots.
- In §14, add a "Construction and rule decisions" row for W5.D7 gating W5.RBR and W6.D0.X509. In the W6.D0.<cap> row, change "none for ... X509" to cite W5.D7.
- Point plan §8.1 (:1199) and the W5 correctness list (:1463) at W5.D7.
- Re-run the machine check: 321 milestones, with the edge count updated.

### F19 [issues-33-43] Plan §5.1 disposition table, pre_state_root/post_state_root row (plan:738); graph W2.4 (graph:364). Lens issue #37.

**Problem.** The disposition authenticates the anchor's post_state_root (FASTPQ new_root) through a result opening of ExecutionCommitment.post_state_root. The code computes FASTPQ new_root as the witnessed-writes SMT root. ExecutionCommitment.post_state_root equals that root only when block a carries no KAGEMUSHA top-ups. With top-ups it is kagemusha_post_state_root(count, ordinary_writes_root, top_up_root). The root that always equals new_root in a block with writes, which every AXT source block has, is ordinary_writes_root. As specified, a valid AXT spend whose source block also carries a top-up would be rejected deterministically.

**Fix.** Fix plan:738 and W2.4 (graph:364) as follows.

- old_root (anchor pre_state_root) is authenticated against ExecutionCommitment.parent_state_root opened from R_a.
- new_root (anchor post_state_root) is authenticated against the ordinary_writes_root opened from R_a, not against ExecutionCommitment.post_state_root.
- State the precondition this relies on. ordinary_writes_root equals the witnessed root only when block a's writes are non-empty (sumeragi/commitment.rs:137-141). The mandatory D7 source write guarantees this for every AXT source block (state.rs:37024-37026). The verifier should reject an anchor whose block has no D7 write.
- Add a note that post_state_root equals ordinary_writes_root only when kagemusha_top_up_root is None. Otherwise it is kagemusha_post_state_root(count, ordinary_writes_root, top_up_root) (data_model sumeragi_finality/commitment.rs:209-216).
- Optionally rename the anchor field, for example to witnessed_post_root, so it is not confused with the combined root. Per first-release policy, add no alias.
- Add a W2.4 KAT and a W2.6i end-to-end case: a source block that carries a KAGEMUSHA top-up next to the AXT transfer must be admitted exactly once.
- Add a mutation test: binding new_root to ExecutionCommitment.post_state_root must fail that top-up case.

prior_findings.summary: AXT binds its FASTPQ new_root to the wrong root when a source block has KAGEMUSHA top-ups.
prior_findings.rationale: Bind FASTPQ old_root to the certified parent_state_root and new_root to certified ordinary_writes_root, with the mandatory D7 source occurrence proving nonempty writes. Keep the combined KAGEMUSHA post_state_root distinct. Add a positive co-occurring top-up transfer case and a mutation that substitutes the combined root.

Because latency terms moved to W5.E2 on the gated network, the X509 construction milestone W5.5 has the integration milestone W5.I1 as an ancestor. ### F25 [issues-55-65] Graph A-checklist (ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md:101-107), A3 record binding (:60-75), Q-checklist item 6 (:99), W6.IC (:503), W6.REL.A (:509); plan §0 Activati

**Problem.** This is a new contradiction from the #63 fix. Under the default M2 train, W6.REL.A installs the W6.IC release on Minamoto, and on Taira for any capability not yet active there. It then activates every qualified capability with 'a W6.G record signed for that network'. The rules forbid that. The record body is produced at qualification and binds that qualification's snapshot digest, binary digests and W6.P candidate-record digest. The A-checklist requires the target network to run 'a release whose W6.P candidate record equals the record's snapshot'. The §0 activation gate requires a network that 'already runs the qualified release'. W6.IC is a later snapshot that includes the deletions, so it never equals any capability's qualification snapshot. No step re-issues the qualification records against W6.IC. No step re-measures the Q-checklist item 3 budgets on W6.IC with W6.MB receipts: W6.IC runs W6.P and delta reviews only. The same gap hits Taira: once a newer release is installed, a capability that qualified but was not yet activated can no longer satisfy its own record. So the default Minamoto activation path cannot be executed under the plan's own rules.

**Fix.** Add a re-binding step for each capability: either inside W6.IC or as a new qualification node W6.IC.Q that depends on W6.IC and is a parent of W6.REL.A. For every qualified capability not yet active on some production-class network, it produces a fresh record body with A3 fields. That body binds the W6.IC source snapshot digest, per-platform binary digests and W6.IC W6.P candidate-record digest. It also binds the capability and shared module-set digests, plus the digests of the original review reports and of each closed delta review. It attaches source-current W6.MB receipts that meet the capability's budget decision (Q-item 3) on W0.D4, and on each W0.D5/W5.D5 platform where wallets prove. For X509 it recomputes the soundness, resource and KAT certificate digests on the W6.IC snapshot. Its sequence number is above any earlier record for that capability. W6.REL.A item (4) then activates with these re-bound records, signed for each network. Also amend three rules: Q-checklist item 6, A-checklist bullet 1, and the plan §0 Activation row and §9.8. A record may name a release later than its qualification snapshot only through this re-binding: the I-checklist and rollback leg pass on that release, the module sets match or the delta review is closed, and the budget receipts are re-measured. Add the Taira rule: a qualified capability is either activated before the next release is installed on that network, or re-bound to the running release under the same conditions before activation. Align W6.RB (2)/(5) ("record for the running release") with the same re-binding definition.

### F26 [issues-55-65] Graph W6.MB (:557), Q-checklist item 3 (:96), W0.D4 (:298); plan §9.5 (:1580-1582)

**Problem.** #55 is only partly resolved. Q-checklist item 3 requires proof size, prover time, memory and verifier time, each with a source-current W6.MB receipt. The W6.MB receipt fields contain no verifier time. Prover time exists only as W6.M phase seconds, and W6.M instruments only FASTPQ provers, so Orchard, FCMP++, PGC, VeRange, Jindo, Bootle/Lantern and Vega have no receipt source for prover time. #55's fix also required every budget receipt to carry host load. W0.D4 and W6.MB do not require it; only W5.E0 and W5.5 record host load. The plan itself cites the non-quiet epoch25 host as a reason receipts cannot be compared.

**Fix.** Make the same edit to W6.MB in the graph (graph:557) and in plan §9.5 (plan:1580-1582).

1. Expand the receipt fields to: source digest, binary digest, the W0.D4 or W0.D5 machine record identifier, protocol and parameter-set identifier, and workload/shape identifier (the maximum shape from the budget decision).
2. Add total prover wall seconds, measured by the builder for every protocol. For FASTPQ adapters, also include the W6.M phase tree (unattributed time at most 1%). For non-FASTPQ protocols (Orchard/Halo2, FCMP++, PGC, VeRange, Jindo, Bootle/Lantern, Vega, and ZK-AMS unless W7.ZA.d picks FASTPQ FRI), wall seconds alone, with no phase tree required.
3. Add verifier seconds at the same shape, plus proof size, prover peak RSS and verifier peak RSS.
4. For server runs: worker count, host load and the concurrent process inventory at start, at least once during and at the end, and a statement that no other proving or compilation ran on the host. For device runs: thread count and thermal state.
5. Add to the completion criterion: "Each receipt carries every quantity that the capability's budget decision bounds; a qualification whose budget names a quantity absent from its receipt fails Q-checklist item 3."

In W0.D4 (graph:298), add: "Every evidence and budget receipt carries this record's machine identifier and a host-load record (host load and concurrent process inventory at start, during and at the end; device receipts record thread count and thermal state)."

Optionally reword Q-checklist item 3 (graph:96) to point at these fields.

**Problem.** The #64 fix asked that, under the authenticated-snapshot option, WG.6's replay criterion become replay from the snapshot. WG.6 now says replay 'from genesis ... or from the network's W6.REL.H authenticated boundary where one is in force'. 3. Add to WG.6: where W6.REL.H records option (b) for a network on which WG is activated before that network's boundary (the M1 train in W6.REL.D item 4), WG.6 closes only after H4 is qualified on a candidate that contains the WG code. On that candidate, a node restored from an authenticated snapshot at a height of at least E must reproduce:
   - StateCommitmentPolicyV1, including pending_change;
   - finalized_state_roots, with exactly min(h - E, W_MAX) entries;

4. Bring plan §4.5 Restart (:611-615) into line with this. Replay starts from genesis, or from the network's W6.REL.H boundary where one is in force. Snapshot restoration is owned by S9/H4, with the M1 plus (b) WG restore test above.

**Problem.** The #57 resolution rests on an assumption the plan does not secure. It keeps the catalog unchanged on the grounds that the preimage and commitment 'do not change' and 'nothing in this plan needs that'. The catalog commitment, however, is a natively computed six-lane GoldilocksDigest384V1 carried in iroha_data_model consensus types. W0.5 leaves its native or in-circuit class open ('classified in the inventory with a named owner'). W0.X1 requires that rg find GoldilocksDigest384V1 in no iroha_data_model consensus type except in-circuit uses that are kept.    - Widen W0.X1's exception clause so it explicitly admits this pinned native catalog constant. Today the clause admits only in-circuit uses and FASTPQ-internal transcript uses, so listing the constant alone does not satisfy W0.X1.

   - Reword W7.0 to "membership and preimage do not change". The commitment changes only at that milestone.

RAM-LFE/FHE, SoraCloud and the W7 protocols.' Most W7 protocols are not FASTPQ adapters: Orchard (Halo2), FCMP++, PGC, VeRange, Jindo, Bootle/Lantern and Vega. §3.2 places non-STARK systems outside FASTPQ consolidation. ### F34 [issues-66-76] #72: plan §4.2 (plan:527), §4.6 (plan:629-630), §4.2 limit-decrease notice (plan:537), WG.1 item (14) (graph:306) versus plan §0 Rollback (plan:162-164), §9.3 (

**Problem.** WG now has two activation and deactivation mechanisms with conflicting rules. §4.2 says 'WG is active at height h iff the singleton exists', and §4.6 and WG.1(14) make deactivation 'a governed removal with notice ≥ W', so in-flight transactions are not invalidated. W6.G instead gives WG a PrivacyProtocolLifecycleV1 record, and A11 and W6.RB let governance suspend it 'at once', with resumption by a signed record. The plan never says what a Suspended WG does.

**Fix.** 1. In WG.1 (new item next to 14) and W6.RB(4), add a WG entry that defines two predicates and their scope:
   - WG_published(h) = the StateCommitmentPolicyV1 singleton exists in S'_h, with WG's lifecycle Active or Suspended. It controls the presence of state_commitment_root (§4.1), the insertion and pruning of finalized_state_roots (§4.2) and keyed-tree maintenance.
   - WG_admitting(h) = WG_published(h) AND lifecycle Active. It controls the §4.3 predicate, the availability of AssertStateWitnessV1 and anchored admission for AXT and IvmProved.
   - While Suspended, AssertStateWitnessV1 and anchored transactions get a typed deterministic rejection inside R, a new reason distinct from 'unavailable on production genesis'.
   - The R layout is unchanged while Suspended, so resuming needs no tree rebuild and no build-time notice.
   - Anchors at heights inside the Suspended interval become admissible after resumption if they are within W.
   - Retired, or removal of the singleton, stops root publication from its effective height.
2. Reconcile the notice rules in §4.6, WG.1 item 14 and A11/W6.RB(2):
   - Active->Suspended takes effect at once, as an incident tightening, with no ≥ W notice.
   - The ≥ W notice in §4.2 and §4.6 applies only to limit decreases and to Retired/singleton removal.
   - Say explicitly whether an incident Retired may skip the notice.
   - The dependency rule stays "W2 and W3 suspended or retired first, or in the same transaction".
3. State the expected WG behaviour for the W6.RB(8) rollback leg that WG.Q already runs through Q-checklist item 4. Optionally mirror it in WG.8. The test checks:
   - roots are still published and certified while Suspended;
   - AssertStateWitnessV1 gets the typed rejection on all 4 validators;
   - Suspended->Active with a newer record restores admission without a rebuild;
   - restart and replay reproduce R across the suspend/resume heights.

### F35 [issues-66-76] #72: W6.RB items (4) and 'Unit tests cover (1)-(6) for every capability id' (graph:507); plan §9.6 (plan:1603-1605), §0 (plan:167); W6.REL.R (graph:508); W6.R.W

**Problem.** #72's fix item 1, an exit path per capability, has no milestone that can deliver it, and Retired is not covered. W6.RB requires every capability's suspended-state declaration (shielded notes, RAM-LFE bindings, pending AXT spends, X509 credentials, SoraCloud jobs), signed by 'the capability's W6.D0 reviewer', and unit tests for every capability id. But W6.RB depends only on W6.G and W6.H, and it must close before W6.REL.R, which every capability qualification except W1.Q.FPQ depends on. So W6.RB either closes without those declarations, or it holds every qualification (including WG.Q and W1.Q.RACE) until the last W7 protocol has a descriptor.

**Fix.** Narrow W6.RB to the generic mechanics. Its unit tests cover (1)-(3), (5) and (6) over the W6.G id set. For (4), it adds a mandatory Suspended/Retired declaration field to the W6.H descriptor. The verifier refuses to activate a capability whose descriptor lacks that field, but W6.RB does not supply any capability's declaration. Remove "the capability's W6.D0 reviewer signs the declaration" from W6.RB.

Each capability's integration milestone writes its own declaration and the exit-path tests: W1.5i, W1.6i, W2.6i, W3.I, W4.Ia/Ib/Ic/I4/I7, the W5 integration node and each W7.*.i. The declaration states, for state created under the capability (shielded notes, RAM-LFE bindings, pending AXT spends inside W, X509 credentials, SoraCloud jobs), what happens under Suspended and under Retired. Add it to each W6.D0.<cap> scope and each W6.R.<cap> criterion, so that reviewer reviews it under the R-checklist. Keep Q-checklist item 4 as the per-capability execution of the rollback leg, and make that leg fail on a missing or unreviewed declaration.

For value-bearing capabilities (the W7 shielded pools, AXT, RAM-LFE, X509, SoraCloud), define Retired semantics in the same declaration. The choice is either:
- an exit path that does not use the retired verifier, plus a drain window that W6.RB tests before any -> Retired takes effect; or
- an explicit A9 owner-decision milestone, on which the capability's qualification depends, that accepts stranding.

Apply the same choice to a FASTPQ-incident suspension that cannot be re-qualified.

### F36 [issues-66-76] #72: W6.RB item (7) (graph:507); A11 last bullet (graph:205); plan §0 Rollback (plan:168), §9.6 (plan:1608); A10 (graph:184); plan §4.4 table (plan:589-600)

**Problem.** #72's fix item 5 is resolved incorrectly. For failures 'where governance cannot commit', W6.RB(7) prescribes 'a signed recovery release through the runtime-upgrade or W6.REL.H path'. The issue asked for an out-of-band operator runbook. The runtime-upgrade path needs a committed ActivateRuntimeUpgrade, which is impossible on a halted chain. The W6.REL.H path is a reset, or an authenticated snapshot that needs the unimplemented S9/H4. On Minamoto the only allowed recovery is therefore a relaunch. A10 says every production deployment goes through runtime-upgrade and makes no exception for recovery.

**Fix.** 1. **Define the halt-recovery release and make it A10's one exception.** In A10 (graph:184), W6.REL.D(3) and A11 (graph:205), define it as follows. When a production-class network cannot commit blocks, its operators install a W6.P-signed recovery candidate out of band, outside any on-chain transaction.
   - The candidate must pass the W6.P history-replay check for that network, reproducing every certified R.
   - It must not activate or loosen any capability (A9).
   - Its validity changes apply only from the first height not yet certified.
   - After the chain resumes, the first committed governance actions:
     - record the release through ProposeRuntimeUpgrade and ActivateRuntimeUpgrade (world.rs:11741, 11787);
     - suspend the faulty capability under W6.RB(2)/(3).
   - Record the exception in A10 and W6.REL.D.
   - Keep the W6.REL.H reset as the last resort only. On Minamoto it is an owner-chosen relaunch, since the authenticated snapshot needs H4 (specs/sumeragi_goals.md:55).

2. **Fix the example everywhere it appears.** In W6.RB(7), A11 and §9.6 (plan:1608), match §4.4 (plan:595-596). Use a deterministic execution fault on f+1 or more validators (2 of 4), so no PrepareQC or CommitQC can form, or NodeError::Replay on every validator after a restart. Drop "RecoveryRequired certified-root mismatch". A single-node RecoveryRequired is local and needs no release (specs/sumeragi.md:2867-2870).

3. **Rewrite the W6.RB(7) rehearsal.** On a 4-validator network:
   - induce that fault on at least 2 validators;
   - show that no block commits, including a submitted governance suspension;
   - install the signed recovery candidate out of band and show that the chain resumes;
   - show that restart and replay reproduce every certified R;
   - show that the post-resumption runtime-upgrade record and the suspension commit.
   W6.REL.R reviews this runbook.

### F37 [issues-66-76] #72: W6.RB item (5) '(the A5 list)' and item (3) (graph:507); A5 (graph:116); plan §9.6 (plan:1606)

**Problem.** The FASTPQ incident transaction covers only the A5 list. That list omits W4.A.6b, 6c and THR, which depend on FASTPQ through 6a (W4.Q.6b, 6c and THR have W1.Q.FPQ as an ancestor).
