Optionally, add 6b, 6c and THR to the A5 FASTPQ-dependent list as well, since they rely on the W1.3 checker, which is part of the shared module set. That also keeps their delta-review digests correct. In W6.RB and A11, state that a FASTPQ incident affecting the live q77 transfer/AXT path (block.rs:3567, world.rs:16262, host.rs:6406), which has no W6.G record until the AXT relation leaves q77 at W2.A, is handled by an emergency tightening release under W6.REL.D(3). ### F43 [issues-66-76] #75: plan §1 (plan:186), §12 (plan:1751), W0.D1.WG (graph:288); longest chain (graph:9)

**Problem.** The claims that each owner record gates only its own workstream are true only for direct edges. §1 says 'WG can start as soon as its owner is named, without waiting for the other eight', and W0.D1.WG says 'no other workstream waits on it'. In fact only WG.E starts on W0.D1.WG alone. WG.1 also waits on W0.D1.W6, then W6.D0, then W6.D0.WG (external WG reviewer contracted and scope signed), so auditor procurement sits on the longest chain. W3.E waits on W0.D1.WG and W0.D1.W1.

**Fix.** In §1 (plan:186), §5 (plan:1725), §12 (plan:1751) and W0.D1.WG (graph:288), change "gates only its own workstream" to "directly gates only its own workstream".

In §1, also state the following:
- WG's first milestone, WG.E, needs only W0.D1.WG plus W0.D4 (named hardware), so it starts without the other eight owner records.
- WG.1 and every later WG milestone also wait on W0.D1.W6, then W6.D0, then W6.D0.WG (WG reviewer contracted and scope signed). This chain is on the longest path (graph:9).

In W0.D1.WG (graph:288), replace "no other workstream waits on it" with: "its only direct dependent is WG.E; downstream, W3 (from W3.E and W3.D1), W2, W1, W0 and W6 milestones wait on it through WG.E and WG.1."

In §12, make the first sentence consistent with the "widest gates" sentence. For example: "No record directly gates every workstream; transitively, W0.D1.W6 and W0.D1.W1 reach all nine, and W0.D4 is the widest direct gate."

### F44 [issues-66-76] #67: W3.E option (b) (graph:374; plan §6.3, plan:869) versus plan §4.7 (plan:646-649) and WG.E2 (graph:316)

**Problem.** This is a residual of #67. W3.E proves STATE_GET in-circuit on W1.1 'for each WG.E candidate hash, reusing WG.E's candidate hash AIRs'. But WG.E's AIRs are constraint-only FixedAir test prototypes that cannot be proven, and porting them to the W1.1 Air trait is WG.E2's job, which covers only the two leading candidates and is not an ancestor of W3.E. So W3.E carries an unstated port of all five candidate hashes.

**Fix.** Choose one of these.

(A) Preferred: limit the in-circuit work to WG.E2's candidates. Add WG.E2 to W3.E's depends_on. This creates no cycle: WG.E2 depends only on W1.1 and WG.E, and W3.E's dependents (W3.D1, W3.D2, W3.D3) already wait for WG.1. Then:
- Rewrite option (b)'s STATE_GET bullet at plan:869 and graph:374 to read: "STATE_GET verifying one inclusion path in-circuit for each of the two WG.E2 candidates, reusing WG.E2's W1.1 State-witness AIRs."
- Add: "For the remaining WG.E candidates, the STATE_GET cost is a projection from WG.E's committed cells per hash, labelled as extrapolated with its derivation."
- Add W3.E to WG.E2's dependents at plan:661 ("WG.E2 also gates W2.4, W3.5 and W3.E") and at plan:1900. Update the graph edge counts.

(B) Keep W3.E independent of WG.E2. Change "reusing WG.E's candidate hash AIRs" to: "porting each WG.E candidate's constraint definitions (WG.E's FixedAir prototypes are test-only base-field evaluators, compact_protocol.rs:37-58, 90-91) to the W1.1 Air trait as part of W3.E's own scope, for all five candidates." Also state that the two WG.E2 candidates share one W1.1 implementation between W3.E and WG.E2, whichever lands first, so the port is not done twice.

In either case, correct the plan §4.7 citation from compact_protocol.rs:91-92 to :90-91.

### F49 [issues-77-87] Issue #82 residual. Graph W1.5 (graph:331), W0.5 (graph:280), W7.AC.e (graph:634)

**Problem.** r5 correctly splits native from in-circuit uses and adds W7.AC.e/W7.AC.d. Three points remain.
- W1.5 still mandates 'Digest384' for the RaceV1 FASTPQ adapter. The verified fix said RaceV1's digest is not in-circuit and that the adapter should use FASTPQ's commitment and transcript hash. The FASTPQ shared API uses SHA3-256 Merkle multiproofs and the W1.1b Keccak duplex sponge, not SHA3-384.
- W0.5 says each native user's milestone 'switches' it to Digest384, but several of those users (the fork, ivm_step_air, privacy transparent_stark.rs, core_zk stark.rs) are deleted, not switched.
- W7.AC.e measures only on the W0.D4 server. The fix required measurements on the mobile reference device as well, and ZK-ACE authorizations are wallet-proven (W7.AC.c records W0.D5 wallet proving).

**Fix.** - **W1.5 (graph:331):** replace "the new adapter uses Digest384 rather than the six-lane digest" with: "its Merkle commitments use the W1.1 shared SHA3-256 Merkle hash and its Fiat-Shamir frames use the W1.1b transcript; any native digest it keeps outside the transcript (today the fork's public-statement digest, execution_proofs/proof.rs:575-593) uses Digest384; no six-lane digest remains in the adapter".
- **W0.5 (graph:280), RaceV1 entry:** reclassify "RaceV1's commitment and Fiat-Shamir use" as "replaced at W1.5 by the W1.1 commitment hash and the W1.1b transcript".
- **W0.5, deleted users:** tag each native user that is removed rather than switched with its deletion milestone:
  - the execution fork and ivm_step_air: W1.X2, after W3.F;
  - iroha_core_zk/src/stark.rs: W1.X4;
  - privacy transparent_stark.rs: W1.X9.
- **W0.5 wording:** change "which its milestone switches to Digest384" to "which its milestone switches to Digest384 or removes".
- **W7.AC.e (graph:634) and plan line 1709:** add W0.D5 to the dependencies. For each candidate hash, also record prover seconds and peak memory for the complete ZK-ACE statement on each W0.D5 device. If the mobile FASTPQ prover path does not exist yet, record a projection derived from measured per-cell device cost and label it as a projection.
- **W7.AC.d:** cite both the server and the device figures.

### F52 [facts-0] §0 'Networks and releases', bullet 'A release never activates anything' (plan:79-83); §9.2 'Release train' (plan ~1513-1515); W6.REL.D item (3); W6.RB item (7) 

**Problem.** The plan says every production-class deployment is a W6.P-signed candidate installed through the runtime-upgrade path, which adds new capability code in the Proposed state. The cited machinery does none of this. The runtime-upgrade path installs no binary or capability code and checks no binary or W6.P digest. It only records a first-release ABI-v1 activation schedule. Taira deployments also go through a different path, the public-reset workflow (a fresh genesis). And a halted chain cannot use this path for recovery, because it needs a committed ActivateRuntimeUpgrade at start_height.

**Fix.** 1. Rewrite §0 (plan:79-83), §9.2 (plan:1512-1514), W6.REL.D(3), A10 and the A-checklist first bullet. Say that a release is a W6.P-signed candidate whose binaries operators deploy out of band. On a chain that keeps its history, the deployment may be announced through an ABI-v1 runtime-upgrade record (specs/runtime_upgrades.md). Its optional SBOM digests and SLSA attestation may carry the W6.P candidate digest. Its provenance signers are governance-policy keys, not W6.P keys. Remove the claim that the runtime-upgrade path installs code or checks W6.P.

2. State that the only binding between a deployment and a candidate the protocol verifies is the W6.G activation record. It binds the W6.P candidate record, the per-platform binary digests and the compiled capability digest of the running binary (plan:104-107). A release that only tightens needs no such binding. W6.REL.D should record whether a runtime-upgrade manifest must also carry the W6.P candidate digest, and who checks it.

3. Name Taira's deployment route as `iroha taira public-reset preflight/apply`, a fresh genesis (sumeragi_taira_reset.md:8-11), and keep the runtime-upgrade record only for Minamoto, or for Taira between resets if the owner chooses that.

4. In W6.RB(7), when governance cannot commit, recovery is a signed recovery release that operators deploy and restart with. It replays certified history, or it uses the W6.REL.H boundary (a fresh genesis or an authenticated snapshot). Drop "runtime-upgrade" as a recovery path there.

### F53 [facts-0] §0 'Networks and releases' (plan:83, citing specs/runbooks/sumeragi_taira_reset.md:15); §9.2 'Release train'; §9.5 W6.P

**Problem.** The plan cites runbook line 15 as consistent with its release model ('deployment policy stays with on-chain governance'). The next sentence of that runbook rules out what the plan imposes. The plan makes W6.P mandatory before every production-class deployment, including focused tests, the four-validator suite, SDK and device runs, and a history-replay check that blocks deployment. The repository's current policy says no mandatory regression suite is a prerequisite for a reset or deployment. The plan neither acknowledges this conflict nor schedules the policy change as an owner decision.

**Fix.** Pick one of two options, and in either case stop citing runbook:15 (plan:83, graph:185, W6.REL.D item 3) as support.

(A) **Make it an explicit owner decision.** Add an item to W6.REL.D in which the owner decides, explicitly, to make a W6.P-signed candidate, its delta check and its history-replay check prerequisites for deploying to Taira and Minamoto. Add a milestone, with W6.P depending on it, that amends in the same change:
- specs/runbooks/sumeragi_taira_reset.md §1 (:15-17)
- specs/sumeragi.md §12.6 (:2888-2889) and §13.5 (:3570-3580)
- specs/sumeragi_goals.md S7 (:38)
- AGENTS.md:222-225

The amended text should state that the prerequisite applies only to these checks, and that diagnostics and soak tests stay optional. The Minamoto leg of W0.9 (a release shown to replay Minamoto's certified blocks) must cite the same decision.

(B) **Reword the plan so that W6.P gates only qualification and activation.** Make the change at plan:79-83, §9.2 (:1512), §9.5 (:1589-1592), graph A10 (:184-185), W6.REL.D item 3 and the W6.P criteria:
- Q-checklist item 4 and the A-checklist (graph:97, :102-103) keep W6.P as a gate.
- The delta and history-replay results go into the candidate record as information for governance's deployment decision. They no longer state that a release "is deployable only across" a boundary.
- Certified-history soundness for deletions is enforced through the W6.REL.H-dependent completion criteria of the deletion milestones, W6.IC and W6.REL.A.

### F54 [facts-0] §9.3 W6.G 'X509 availability moves to protocol state' (plan:1533-1540); W6.G test (i) in the graph

**Problem.** The plan claims that once W6.G moves X509 availability to protocol state, 'Integration networks then run X509, and the four-validator gate (privacy_exact12_zk_x509_network.rs:971-979) can start'. Two code facts block this. First, the gate test reads an installed resource-certificate fixture that does not exist. Second, admitting any catalog proof, X509 included, requires the immutable Exact12 qualification singleton (the all-twelve rule), which is removed only at W7.0, and W7.0 depends on W6.G. So W6.G's completion test (i) cannot pass at W6.G.

**Fix.** 1. **W6.G(i), graph and §9.3 prose.** Limit it to: on the same binary, an integration network whose genesis roots verify an integration-signed record moves X509 from Proposed to Active, and its capability row shows the compiled profile Available with zero pins. A production-profile genesis refuses: X509 stays Proposed with no record, and the profile is not taken from the pins. Remove the clause "Integration networks then run X509, and the four-validator gate (privacy_exact12_zk_x509_network.rs:971-979) can start." State that X509 proof admission (`SubmitPrivacyProofV1`) is still refused at W6.G, because the Exact12 singleton is required (privacy_state.rs:116-117, all-twelve rule :186-206) until W7.0.

2. **W5.I1 (depends on W7.0).** Make it the milestone where privacy_exact12_zk_x509_network.rs is rewritten and passes. W5.I1:
   - replaces the installed source-pinned resource certificate (:93-94, :150-170, :980-983), which needs a non-zero `ZK_X509_RESOURCE_CERTIFICATE_SHA256_V1` (readiness_certificates.rs:91, :916-927), with the certificate digests carried in the integration-signed W6.G record (zero allowed only under integration roots);
   - replaces the `MissingProductionQualification` expectations (:1124-1131, :1287-1290, :1421-1426) and the Exact12 admission path with the W7.0 per-protocol record;
   - requires the canonical action to be applied and the malformed one rejected.

3. **Plan line 1445 and W5.E2.** Keep citing W5.I1 as the first network that admits an X509 proof.

Keep privacy.rs:45-60 only to identify the catalog members.

2. Add one sentence after plan:117-119: "Proof admission for a catalog protocol also requires the immutable Exact12 qualification singleton, registered once under CanEnactGovernance (isi/privacy.rs:441-477). It binds all twelve protocols at once, and W7.0 removes it in favour of per-protocol W6.G records."

3. Optionally, add a note to the X509 row (plan:134) that X509 is a catalog member and is held by the same singleton gate.

### F66 [facts-2] Plan §5.1 anchor table, row `pre_state_root`, `post_state_root`, and the 'FASTPQ roots' bullet (also §4.3 'execution-witness roots')

**Problem.** The plan says the AXT/FASTPQ `new_root` (the anchor's `post_state_root`) is authenticated by opening `ExecutionCommitment.post_state_root` from R_a. In the code those two values are different whenever the source block carries KAGEMUSHA top-ups. In that case R's `post_state_root` is the combined top-up root, while FASTPQ `new_root` is the plain witnessed-write root. Following the plan, the equality check would reject valid spends from such blocks, or a relation would bind the wrong root.

**Fix.** Change the §5.1 row to read: "`pre_state_root` is authenticated as equal to the opened `ExecutionCommitment.parent_state_root`. `post_state_root`, which is FASTPQ `new_root` (the witnessed-write root), is authenticated as equal to the opened `ordinary_writes_root`, not to `ExecutionCommitment.post_state_root`. The two differ when block a carries KAGEMUSHA top-ups (iroha_core sumeragi/commitment.rs:134-151)."

Two notes support this:
- A source block with a successful transfer always has non-empty writes. In that case `ordinary_writes_root` equals the witnessed root (commitment.rs:137-141). The verifier should reject an opened `ordinary_writes_root` equal to the empty-tree root `Hash::new([])` (smt.rs:193).
- No recomputation of the combined root is needed. `ExecutionCommitment::validate` (data_model commitment.rs:174-200) already binds `post_state_root` to `ordinary_writes_root` and the top-up root and count for every certified R.

Make the same correction in three other places:
- the 'FASTPQ roots' bullet (plan:745-746);
- §4.3's opening bullet (plan:561), so it names which opened field corresponds to `new_root`;
- the W2.4 completion criterion in the graph (dag_r5_final.json:705).

Add two tests to W2.4's acceptance:
- a positive end-to-end test in which the source block carries at least one KAGEMUSHA top-up receipt next to the AXT source transfer;
- a negative test showing that substituting the combined `post_state_root` for `new_root` is rejected, which also covers the reverse substitution.

prior_findings.rationale: Authenticate new_root through ordinary_writes_root and bind the D7 source transfer; independently respect the certified combined-root relation. Add positive top-up coexistence and negative root-substitution tests; canonical V1 types should name distinct roots clearly without aliases.

### F67 [facts-2] Plan §4.5 Serving: 'Config validation warns when it is below W'

**Problem.** This cannot be implemented as stated. W is protocol state (`StateCommitmentPolicyV1`, §4.2) and is known only after genesis or Kura replay. `iroha_config` validation runs before State exists and cannot read W.

**Fix.** Replace the sentence in §4.5 (plan:605-606), and the matching clause in WG.5 (milestone graph.md:310 and dag_r5_final.json:221), with: "R_serve is compared with W only after replay. Once `node::prepare` has rebuilt State, startup logs a warning if R_serve < W of the committed head. The check follows the post-replay pattern of `validate_sumeragi_key_policy` (irohad main.rs:2972) but only warns and never fails startup. Torii status and telemetry also report R_serve, the current W and any scheduled `pending_change`. They raise an R_serve < W signal at a W change's scheduled height and again at its effective height. Config-only validation (`validate_config`, `validate_config_offline`) checks only R_serve's own bounds, because W is protocol state and is never read from `iroha_config`." Add a WG.5/WG.8 test: a node with R_serve below the new W shows the warning signal after a governed increase of W, and validity is unchanged.

### F71 [facts-3] §6.5 finalized_prestate row ("recomputed from the certified header ... bind every context sysvar (block height, time, VRF seed)"); §6.7 syscall table row "Conte

**Problem.** VRF_EPOCH_SEED is not a header-derived context value. Core reads it from world State: it projects the `global_beacon_pulses` table using `sumeragi_npos_parameters`. The lookup is keyed by epoch and has a fallback to the latest epoch, so it is in effect a range read. The certified header cannot bind it. It needs WG inclusion/range witnesses and an access-transcript entry. That puts it in the ledger-reads class, which is part of the W3.D3 floor. Classing it as an A9-excludable context sysvar is therefore wrong as well.

**Fix.** Make these changes to revision 5.

§6.7, syscall table:
- Move VRF_EPOCH_SEED from "Context sysvars" (10 → 9) to "Ledger reads and queries" (17 → 18), marked "No (floor)".

§6.5, `finalized_prestate` row:
- Change the header-recomputed list to header-sourced values only: block height and block time / CURRENT_TIME_MS.
- Add one sentence: VRF_EPOCH_SEED is not a header value. The anchor header's `global_beacon_pulse_hash` (header.rs:86-89) binds only that block's own pulse.

§6.5, `access_dependencies` row:
- State that each VRF_EPOCH_SEED call is bound by WG.5 witnesses against `complete_state_root`.
- The witnesses cover the reads that host.rs:4307-4366 and beacon.rs:2766-2806 actually perform:
  - a point read of `sumeragi_npos_parameters` (epoch length);
  - point reads of `global_beacon_pulses`, `global_beacon_pulse_slots` and `global_beacon_key_sessions` for the boundary pulse;
  - the canonical anchor block-hash check. That check currently reads `state.block_hashes()`, so W3.5 must either show that this table is under `complete_state_root` or bind it through the WG.4 finalized-root history;
  - for `fallback_to_latest` (host.rs:5580-5590), a complete range or absence observation proving that no later valid boundary pulse exists up to the anchor height. Conflict removal (host.rs:4361-4364) must also be provable.

### F72 [facts-3] §6.1 'Where the code is today'; §6.4 enforcement bullet; §6.7 'Hash, signature and AEAD' row (SM2_VERIFY, SM4_GCM_SEAL)

**Problem.** Today the semantics of the six SM helper syscalls depend on node crypto configuration and on the `sm` Cargo feature: they either return PermissionDenied or execute. §6.4 says W3 enforcement never comes from node config or a Cargo feature, and every syscall is proven by default. But §6 does not record this existing config/feature gate, and it does not name the protocol-state source the relation must use for these syscalls.

**Fix.** 1. Add a row to §6.1: "SM helper syscalls (SM3_HASH, SM2_VERIFY, SM4_GCM/CCM_SEAL/OPEN) are gated by node crypto config and the `sm` Cargo feature. The gate is at host.rs:11257-11273 and :9840 and reads `actual::Crypto::sm_helpers_enabled`, actual.rs:1477-1490. IVM DefaultHost.sm_enabled is set from it. It is pinned to the genesis manifest only by a startup check (irohad main.rs:678-717)."

2. Give one milestone ownership of removing the gate: W0.3, or a new W0 item that W3.5 depends on. Under that milestone:
   - SM-syscall enablement comes from a protocol-state crypto record. A candidate is the existing genesis `crypto_manifest_meta` custom parameter (iroha_data_model parameter/system.rs:1820-1824), or a governed successor to it.
   - Enablement never comes from `actual::Crypto` or `cfg(feature = "sm")`.
   - The SM code paths compile unconditionally (AGENTS.md:106).

3. In W3.5, the relation and the reference host take SM enablement from that record. When SM is disabled, the relation proves the `PermissionDenied` outcome.

4. Add a W3.I test, mirroring W0.3's `[zk]` test: two validators with different local crypto config produce identical R for IvmProved transactions that call the SM syscalls, under both an SM-enabled and an SM-disabled test genesis.

### F76 [facts-4] Plan §7.1 row 9 (SoraCloud production support); the same short list is repeated in the §0 'Production refusals stay until activation' table

**Problem.** The row lists one core call site and two data-model refusal methods as 'the' SoraCloud production-support refusals. The repo has many more: 12 core ISI call sites, five data-model refusal methods, and three state-restore refusals. W4.7 is meant to turn these refusals into a protocol-state gate and W4.A.SC to lift them. Built from this row, that would leave FHE secrets, FHE state bindings, deployment bundles and persisted deployment state hard-refused after activation. A node could then fail to restore its own post-activation state. Row 1 lists the RAM-LFE restore path (deserialize_core.rs:2271-2283); row 9 has no equivalent.

**Fix.** Make the same change in four places: Plan §7.1 row 9, the §0 refusal table row, graph W4.7 (and the A2 list at graph md:49), and graph W6.O.SC.

1. List every refusal method and what it refuses:
   - fhe.rs:901-903 (FheExecutionPolicyV1, always).
   - fhe.rs:3047-3051 (SecretEnvelopeEncryptionV1, the FheCiphertext variant).
   - fhe.rs:4375-4380 (SoraDeploymentBundleV1, any FHE state binding).
   - schema.rs:2550-2554 (SoraStateEncryptionV1, the FheCiphertext variant only).
   - deployment.rs:400-408 (SoraServiceDeploymentStateV1, any retained fhe_policy_records, including inactive history, plus secret encryption).
2. List every core ISI call site: soracloud.rs:5982, 6443, 6480, 9680, 9685, 10284, 10534, 10694, 10839, 10968, 11168 and 11504.
3. List the restore checks: deserialize_world.rs:183, 235 and 1656-1660.
4. Change "Always refuse" to "Refuse every FHE declaration (Plaintext and ClientCiphertext pass)".
5. State that W4.7 turns all of these, including the restore checks and the fhe_policy_records rule, into one protocol-state gate, and that W4.A.SC lifts all of them. Add a W4.7 test that a post-activation state holding FHE policies, secrets, bindings and entries restores and replays to identical roots. Add a W6.RB case: after Suspended, the retained FHE state still restores.
6. Make W6.O.SC's descoped branch name the full set, not just two items.

### F80 [facts-5] Plan §8.1, table 'The pins W5.L1 changes' (plan lines 1218-1228); the matching W5.L1 acceptance grep is in the milestone graph appendix, line 451

**Problem.** The table is offered as the list of q- and mask-dependent pins, but it leaves out several production pins. The appendix's acceptance grep would not find any of them. The omissions are a CA proof-byte maximum in the verifier geometry gate, the CA byte maxima in accumulator_stark.rs, the DER quotient-degree pins derived from the mask degree, an IO-trace inequality against the mask degree, and the SHA-256 pin of the compact-CA descriptor that is bound into the compiled profile. Each one fails closed (compile-time assert, verifier gate or test), so nothing goes silently wrong. Still, the table is incomplete, and the closure rule (the grep returns only intentional assertions) can pass while these remain stale.

**Fix.** Update the W5.L1 inventory in plan §8.1 (lines 1218-1228) and in appendix row W5.L1 (line 451):
- (d) proof-byte maxima: add aggregate_stark.rs:241 (compact_ca_private_padding_v1 maximum_proof_bytes) and zk_x509/accumulator_stark.rs:348-349 (CA inner and envelope maxima). Recompute each and recheck it against 9,437,184 B, as for the existing entries.
- (b) mask geometry: add zk_x509/der_stark.rs:70-71 and zk_x509/stark.rs:307-308. These are the 1_815 assert and the derived DER maximum quotient degree 3_158_433 = 7*(2^19 + mask) - 2^19.
- Separately, list zk_x509/stark.rs:319-329 (IO minimum trace log 14 against MASK_DEGREE) as an invariant to re-derive at the new q, not as a literal pin.
- (e) descriptors: add zk_x509/air.rs:16-19, ZK_X509_COMPACT_CA_SUBPROOF_DESCRIPTOR_SHA256_V1, bound into the compiled profile at zk_x509/engine.rs:558. Mark it as a digest pin that must be recomputed whenever accumulator_stark.rs:226 changes. Today only the test at air.rs:314-316 checks it.

Change the closure rule so the grep is not the only check. Add a checklist entry for literals the grep cannot match: byte maxima, quotient degrees derived from the mask, and descriptor digests. Also require the full zk_x509 test suite, including the air.rs digest test, to pass at the new q.

### F85 [facts-6] Plan §10 Shared W7 milestones, W7.D1, line 1689

**Problem.** W7.D1 is framed against the wrong code. It says that under 'yes' "ML-KEM-768 replaces X25519 in the note family", but PQ-MASP, one of the two note-family members, already uses ML-KEM-768. Only the IVM private note (and the atomic-settlement audit wrap) uses X25519. The 'no' outcome is also not addressed. The IVM private note is committed in the catalog as pq-qrom even though its on-chain note encryption is classical X25519. The catalog type documents that the label records the weakest primitive in the composition. Correcting the label would change the catalog preimage and commitment that §10 says this plan never needs to change.

**Fix.** Restate W7.D1 in both the plan (line 1689) and the graph (line 566).

**Yes:** ML-KEM-768 replaces X25519 in the IVM private-note wallet codec (ivm_private_note/wallet.rs). Settlement-leg outputs use that codec (atomic_private_settlement/wallet.rs:54), so they are covered too. PQ-MASP already uses ML-KEM-768. The settlement audit wrap is already hybrid X25519 + ML-KEM-768 (audit.rs:42) and stays unchanged. The existing pq-qrom label for IrohaIvmPrivateNoteStarkV1 is then consistent.

**No:** X25519 stays, and the decision record must resolve the pq-qrom label of IrohaIvmPrivateNoteStarkV1 (privacy.rs:57). Either:
- (a) An A9 owner decision narrows the documented meaning of `PrivacySecurityModelV1` (privacy.rs:244-248) to soundness and authorization, and the plan states that this protocol's note confidentiality is classical. Or:
- (b) An A9 owner decision changes the label to classical-rom, with the catalog preimage and commitment regenerated (privacy.rs:45-60; iroha_crypto/src/privacy.rs:13-21). §10's statement "the catalog is not extended" is then amended to allow this one label change.

Make W6.D0.NF's signed scope cover the chosen label resolution. Make W7.NF.c's closure check that the label matches the encryption actually built.

### F86 [facts-6] Plan §14 Evidence → decision, E-PT row, line 1904

**Problem.** The security bound "noise within log QP ≤ 868" is stated with no ring dimension, security level, secret distribution or derivation. Nothing in the repo supports it. The usual HE-standard figure for N = 2^15 with a ternary secret at 128-bit classical security is 881, so 868 needs a cited estimator run or table, or a label as illustrative.

**Fix.** 1. In plan §14 line 1904, state the parameters next to the bound: "noise within log QP ≤ 868 (candidate: N = 2^15, uniform ternary secret, 128-bit classical; illustrative until W4.D0 records the derivation)".
2. Make the source explicit in one of two ways. Either cite the HomomorphicEncryption.org 2018 security standard table, which gives 881 for these parameters, and state why 868 was chosen (for example a margin or a refined estimator), or cite a lattice-estimator run by commit or version, with its cost model, secret and error distributions, and classical-versus-quantum target.
3. In the appendix, add to the W4.D0 completion criteria (line 398) that specs/fhe_rns_bfv.md records the log QP bound's derivation (estimator version, cost model, distributions, security target). Have W4.E1 (line 400) check against "the W4.D0-recorded bound" instead of a hard-coded 868, so that the figure enters a pass/fail budget only once its derivation is recorded.

### F94 [consistency] Plan §13 Activation clause, plan:1826-1827; appendix W0.D2 items (a)-(j), graph.md:284; versus §0 Activation authority, plan:99-116, and A3, graph.md:55-70

**Problem.** The executable objective describes activation as a governance transition that installs the qualified digest. It never mentions the record signed by the release-pinned qualification signers, or the W6.REL.R gate review. §0 and A3 say governance alone can only tighten. As adopted, the objective would permit the governance-only loosening that revision 5 was built to remove (#63, #1, #83).

**Fix.** 1. Rewrite the §13 Activation clause: a loosening transition (Proposed -> Active, Suspended -> Active) is admitted only with a qualification record signed by a threshold of the release-pinned W6.REL.K signer set and verified by W6.G. The record binds the chain id, genesis hash, scope, compiled capability digest and an increasing sequence number. CanEnactGovernance alone only tightens (suspend, retire, one-way refusal). Trust roots are immutable after genesis. A governed transition installs the record, never node config, an environment variable or a Cargo feature.
2. In the §13 Qualification clause, add that every capability qualification except W1.Q.FPQ waits for W6.REL.R closing on the qualified source.
3. Change plan:1833 from "ZK plan r4 milestone graph.md" to "ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md", so that the adopted objective points to the graph that carries the revision-5 A3.
4. Add an item (k) to W0.D2 (graph.md:284): the adopted text states the activation-authority property (signed record, W6.G verification, governance-only tightening, immutable trust roots), names W6.REL.R as a parent of every capability qualification, and cites the current graph revision.

### F95 [consistency] Appendix W0.9 row, graph.md:287; plan §11 row, plan:1737; §12 row, plan:1765; versus A10, graph.md:184-187, §0, plan:79-85, and W6.REL.D item (3), graph.md:504

**Problem.** W0.9 cannot close until its refusal is deployed on Taira and Minamoto, including a Minamoto release that replays Minamoto's certified history. Yet W0.9 depends only on W6.REL.D and W0.D1.W0. A10, §0 and W6.REL.D say every deployment to a production-class network, tightening releases included, is a W6.P-signed candidate that passes the W6.P history-replay check. **Fix.** Both of the finding's options are valid, but each has a cost the plan should state.

(a) Split W0.9.
- W0.9 (construction) keeps the code, the tests and the integration-network and dev-genesis leg (height 1), with its current dependencies [W6.REL.D, W0.D1.W0].
- A new milestone, W0.9.D (activation/deployment), depends on [W0.9, W6.P]. It carries the Taira leg (next reset genesis or governed transition) and the Minamoto leg. The Minamoto leg is a W6.P candidate, built if needed from a patch on Minamoto's deployed release line, whose history-replay check passes for Minamoto. W0.9.D also records the effective heights and the counts of accepted binding-route verifications and registrations.
- The new milestone also needs W6.H, but W6.P already depends on W6.H.
- Re-point W6.IC to W0.9.D. W6.IC needs "the W0.9 refusal is in force", which is the deployed state.
- Leave W1.6, W1.M and W1.X3 on the construction node, unless they need the live height.
- Update §11, §12 (W0.9.D starts after W6.P) and §14.
- Cost: §0's "in production now" (plan:24) must be reworded. The production refusal now waits for W6.P, which itself waits on W0.D5 devices, W0.2, W0.3 and W6.H.

(b) Keep W0.9 whole and make an explicit, narrow exception.
- In A10 (graph.md:184-187), §0 (plan:79-85), §9.2 (plan:1512-1514) and W6.REL.D item (3) (graph.md:504), state that a tightening-only release that comes before W6.P need not be a W6.P-signed candidate.
- Such a release must instead:
  - be a patch on the network's deployed release line that only adds refusals;
  - pass a named stand-alone replay check: a read-only export of the network's certified blocks, replayed by the patched binary, reproduces every certified R. This is the same procedure as W6.P check (2), run ad hoc;
  - have reproducible artifact digests recorded by the W6.REL.D operator role.
- Once W6.P exists, every later tightening release goes through W6.P.
- W0.9's Minamoto criterion then cites this named check instead of an unnamed "release shown to replay".
- This needs an explicit owner decision recorded with W6.REL.D, because it relaxes a stated deployment rule.

### F106 [consistency] Plan §4.1, plan:493-496; appendix WG.1 item (3), graph.md:306; versus A10, graph.md:192, §9.4, plan:1553-1562, and W6.REL.H, graph.md:506

**Problem.** WG.1 decides, for each network with certified history, whether the new ExecutionCommitment layout ships before genesis or the network restarts from a fresh signed genesis. That is a history-boundary decision, which A10 and §9.4 give to W6.REL.H, yet WG.1 has no W6.REL.D or W6.REL.H ancestor and W6.REL.H's list of gated items omits the WG layout change. For Minamoto, whose 'live certified history ... must stay replayable', the only option left is a reset.

**Fix.** 1. **Rewrite WG.1 item (3)** (graph.md:306) and plan §4.1 (plan:493-496). WG.1 should state whether the new ExecutionCommitment encoding leaves the R preimage of pre-activation heights byte-identical. If it does, no boundary is needed. If it does not, WG.1 should defer to W6.REL.H, which chooses for each history-keeping network between a fresh genesis and an authenticated snapshot, instead of WG.1 choosing between pre-genesis shipping and a reset.

2. **Add the edge W6.REL.D -> WG.1**, so WG.1 knows which networks keep their history.

3. **Name the WG.2 ExecutionCommitment layout change** in W6.REL.H's gated list (graph.md:506; plan:1560-1561) and in the §10 row (plan:1883).

4. **Optionally add W6.REL.H -> WG.A** if the WG layout breaks replay on Minamoto under M1. Under M2, W6.REL.A already depends on W6.REL.H.

### F115 [critic-exec] dist/reports/ZK privacy and FHE plan.md:104-109, 165-166, 1533-1534; dist/reports/ZK plan r5 milestone graph.md:63 (A3), 203 (A11); crates/iroha_core_privacy/sr

**Problem.** Every capability record is bound to its compiled capability digest. The plan does not say what happens to an Active or Suspended record when a later release changes that digest, yet both the per-capability train and incident recovery depend on such releases.

**Fix.** Specify the change in W6.REL.K, W6.G and W6.RB, with matching edits to A3, A11 and plan §0 Rollback / §9.3.

1. **Store the digest in protocol state; check the binary only from the upgrade height.**
   - Each record stores its bound compiled capability digest and the height from which it is effective.
   - At or above that height, block-start planning and proof verification compare only the current Active record with the running binary's compiled constants.
   - Replay of historical install and transition transactions (today privacy.rs:211, :259) checks the signed record bytes and the stored digest. It does not check the current binary's constants.
   - Restore (privacy_state.rs:371) and block-start planning (privacy_state.rs:295, :330) stop rejecting Suspended and Retired records, and Active records below a pending rebind height, as "not compiled".

2. **Explicit upgrade rule for a release that changes an Active capability's compiled digest.**
   - Default: the capability must already be Suspended before the runtime upgrade's activation height. Alternatively, the upgrade suspends it automatically at that height, as a tightening step.
   - A W6.P check fails any candidate that changes the digest of a capability Active on a target network without one of these two.
   - A new signed record with a higher sequence, bound to the new digest, resumes the capability after the upgrade height.
   - Add a governed re-bind transition. Today registration refuses a second record (AlreadyRegistered, privacy.rs:214), and a transition copies every digest field (privacy.rs:257).

3. **The incident path (A11; W6.RB item 5) uses this rule.**
   - The incident transaction suspends the capabilities.
   - The patched release activates through the runtime-upgrade path.
   - The re-qualified record resumes them.
   - The plan states which W6.REL.H boundary, if any, applies when the patch changes verification of proofs already in certified history.

4. **Tests.**
   - W6.G: a 4-validator network moves from release N to N+1 with a changed digest. It checks:
     - a binary installed ahead of activation keeps processing blocks;
     - the Suspended record survives restart;
     - resumption with the new record succeeds;
     - an Active capability without suspension blocks the candidate;
     - replay from genesis with N+1 reproduces every certified R.
   - W6.RB: the incident leg runs across a real release change.
   - W6.P: the digest-change check, and history replay across the rebind.

### F124 [critic-security] Plan §0 Activation authority (lines 101-115, esp. 114-115), §4.2 'Where it lives' (527-528), §9.2 genesis-set objects (1519-1522); graph A3 (line 69), W6.REL.D 

**Problem.** Genesis on a production-class (pinned) chain can enable a capability without any signed qualification record, contradicting the plan's central guarantee that no capability is enabled without the release-pinned signatures. WG activity is defined as singleton existence 'set in genesis', and W6.REL.D routes StateCommitmentPolicyV1 through 'a new genesis'. Taira resets with a fresh genesis routinely. W6.REL.A allows 'a fresh genesis built from it' and then signs records only for capabilities 'not yet active there', so anything active from genesis skips the record. A repository tool already emits a Taira height-1 genesis that activates all 12 privacy protocols, and the plan neither mentions nor retires it. W6.G tests reject integration roots in a production genesis, but not an Active lifecycle, a WG policy singleton or an open gate in a production genesis.

**Fix.** 1. **A3, W6.REL.K and §0.** Add item (6): a genesis for a pinned chain id is invalid if it contains any of the following:
   - a loosening TransitionPrivacyProtocolLifecycleV1, or any capability lifecycle other than Proposed;
   - any W6.G qualification record;
   - a StateCommitmentPolicyV1 singleton;
   - any capability gate in its open state.

   State that the W6.G record check in loosening transitions has no is_initial_genesis_context exemption. The governance-only genesis bypass in ensure_privacy_governance (isi/privacy.rs) does not extend to it.

2. **§4.2 and WG.1.** On pinned chains, WG becomes active only through WG.A's post-genesis, W6.G-verified transition. "Set in genesis" applies only to non-pinned integration chains. Also reconcile the singleton-existence test with WG's W6.G lifecycle: the singleton exists iff WG's lifecycle is Active.

3. **§9.2 and W6.REL.D item 5.** Remove StateCommitmentPolicyV1 from the genesis-set objects for production-class networks. Widen WG.3's sentence to every production-class network, Taira resets included.

4. **W6.REL.A.** Item (3) excludes StateCommitmentPolicyV1. Item (4) becomes: every capability is activated by a post-genesis W6.G record signed for that network's current genesis hash, including after a relaunch or reset.

5. **W6.G tests.** Add test (k): a production-profile genesis that carries an Active lifecycle, a W6.G record or a WG singleton fails validation, while an integration genesis carrying the WG singleton is accepted.

6. **W7.0 (or W6.G).** Retire or rewrite kagami emit-taira-v1/validate-taira-v1 (privacy_bootstrap.rs:45-47, 136-142, 196-215) and configs/soranexus/taira/privacy_bootstrap_plan.json / privacy_rollout_plan_v1.json, which emit height-1 Active transitions.

7. **§4.1 (plan:481).** LtHash retirement on a WG-active-from-genesis chain cannot happen on a pinned chain without a new owner (A9) decision.

### F125 [critic-security] Plan §0 objective (45) and refusal table confidential_v2 row (136), §3.2 scope (383); graph W0.9 (287), W7.CV.c (614)

**Problem.** Several Halo2 proof paths are live in production today and sit outside the gate model: no review, qualification, W6.G record, refusal row or A9 decision. They are Kaigi authorization/usage and the confidential transfer/unshield circuits. Proofs reach them through generic VerifyProof, the IVM verify syscalls, ZK_VERIFY_BATCH, RegisterZkAsset verifier bindings and Kaigi privacy mode, with verifying-key registration gated only by a grantable permission. 'No production admission precedes qualification' therefore does not hold for them. The refusal table's claim that confidential_v2 stays refused until W7.CV.A is wrong, because its circuits are in the production Halo2 registry now.

**Fix.** 1. Add a "Live non-STARK proof paths" inventory to §0 and §3.2, with file:line for each path:
   - Kaigi ZkRosterV1 authorization and usage, verified at kaigi/privacy.rs:84-110 and 200-222, with the VK named in iroha_config actual.rs:10500-10503.
   - Production verification of the confidential transfer/unshield circuits through generic VerifyProof (world.rs:13377-13422), the IVM verify syscalls and ZK_VERIFY_BATCH (host.rs:4795-4838, 9940, 11031).
   - RegisterZkAsset vk_unshield binding and the switch to Convertible (world.rs:14121-14215).

**Problem.** The live q77 transfer and AXT relations gate production value paths but are never treated as capabilities. W6.R.FPQ reviews only the shared machinery, not the AIR semantics of the 923-constraint transfer/AXT relation. W6.R.AXT reviews only the new W2.4 adapter. W1.Q.FPQ 'activates nothing'. The ordinary transfer stays on q77 for the whole first release, and nothing says what happens if the W1.3 derivation for the q77 parameter set misses the target. These relations have no W6.G lifecycle, so a FASTPQ incident cannot suspend them. The delta-review rule triggers only for networks where a W6.G capability is Active, so W1.1, W1.2 and W1.4 rewrites of the live verifier's code can reach Taira/Minamoto releases before W6.R.FPQ and W1.Q.FPQ close.

**Fix.** 1. **Review scope.** Extend W6.D0.FPQ and W6.R.FPQ to cover the AIR semantics of the live q77 relation: the 923 constraints, the boundary rows, and the public-column and transfer/AXT statement binding (`gadgets/public_transfer_statement.rs`, `axt_binding`). An alternative is a separate W6.R.Q77 node that W1.Q.FPQ depends on. Keep W1.Q.FPQ as the qualification W6.IC depends on; no new one is needed.

   - W1.Q.FPQ does not close;
   - the owner either records an A9 decision accepting the lower figure, or starts a replacement-adapter chain (new typed id, integration, qualification, activation, history-replay handling);
   - meanwhile, a tightening release may refuse the affected q77 paths.
3. **Incident handling.** Do one of the following:
   - (a) Give the live q77 transfer/AXT paths a W6.G capability id with a PrivacyProtocolLifecycleV1 lifecycle. It is installed Active by genesis or a governed migration (listed in W6.REL.D) and included in the W6.RB(5) FASTPQ incident transaction. It also declares its Suspended behaviour for fee-sponsor vault allocations and pending AXT proofs.
   - (b) Alternatively, state in A11 and W6.RB that a q77 incident goes through a signed tightening security-fix release, with a rehearsed runbook and a stated time-to-refusal.
4. **Delta check.** Extend A5(c) and W6.P check (1) to treat the live q77 verification path as Active on every production-class network that runs it. No release carrying W1.1, W1.1b, W1.2 or W1.4 changes, or any later shared FASTPQ diff, to modules on that path may reach Taira, or Minamoto under M1, before W6.R.FPQ or its delta review has closed. ### F128 [critic-security] Plan §0 Summary (21) and Activation authority (112-113), §4.2 Changes (533-539); graph W0.3 (278), W0.4 (279), WG.3 (308)

**Problem.** Governance (not a signed record) becomes able to loosen validity, contradicting 'Governance alone can only tighten'. W0.3 moves the consensus ZK parameters on chain but never says which [zk] keys become governed parameters or who may loosen them. Today that consensus-hashed set includes verifying-key references, Poseidon/Pedersen parameter-set ids, proof-size and verify-call limits, and anchor ages. W0.4 makes anchor and bridge-proof ages 'changed only by governed transitions'; the bridge default is 0 = unlimited. WG.3 allows W and cap increases 'in either direction' with no stated authority. Swapping a verifying-key reference or a parameter id changes the accepted relation.

**Fix.** 1. **Classify every parameter.** In W0.3, list each field of the six ZkConsensusPolicyV1 sub-policies (zk_policy.rs:10-160). Classify each field, each W0.4 window and each WG.3 StateCommitmentPolicyV1 limit into one of four classes:
   - (a) Relation-selecting: halo2.enabled and stark.enabled, curve, backend, max_k, poseidon_params_id and pedersen_params_id, kaigi_authorization_vk and kaigi_usage_vk. These are never governance parameters. Each becomes a compiled constant, or a field bound into the owning capability's W6.G record and qualification scope. Changing one needs a new signed record, plus an A9 decision if a guarantee changes.
   - (b) Admission resource limits: proof and envelope bytes, verify calls, public inputs, witness caps, gas. A decrease is tightening, so CanEnactGovernance with notice suffices. An increase is allowed only within a range recorded in the active qualification record, or with a new signed record.
   - (c) Freshness windows: max_anchor_age_blocks, the bridge past-age and future-drift limits, and WG W. An increase is loosening and follows the same rule as (b). Production genesis sets finite bridge ages, and moving to 0 = unlimited counts as loosening.
   - (d) Replay retention: replay_retention_slots and tree_roots_history_len. Here a decrease is loosening. An invariant ties retention to at least the corresponding anchor window.

2. **Reconcile W2.A and plan:792-793 with W6.REL.K item (4).** A "governed increase" of W is admissible by governance alone only up to the W_required, or the W_max, recorded in the consumer's signed qualification record. Anything beyond that needs a signed record.

3. **Extend W6.REL.K and A3.** Define "loosening" so that it covers parameter moves in the loosening direction, not only lifecycle transitions.

4. **Add W6.G tests.**
   - CanEnactGovernance alone is rejected when it raises W, an anchor age or a cap beyond the qualified range, sets a bridge age to 0, lowers replay retention, or swaps a verifying-key reference or parameter id.
   - The tightening direction succeeds with notice.

5. **Extend the review scope.** Put the classification and its enforcement in the W6.D0.GATE scope and in the W6.REL.R R-checklist.

### F129 [critic-security] Plan §0 Activation authority (104-111); graph W6.G (473), A3 (59-68), W6.REL.K (505), W6.P history-replay (474)

**Problem.** Record verification depends on the running binary. The verifier is 'a pure function of committed state, the record bytes and compiled constants'; the record binds 'the compiled capability digest of the running binary'; signer keys are compiled in, and rotating them needs a new release. Replay re-executes every block, so a later release that rotates signers or changes a capability's compiled digest re-checks historical activation records against new constants and rejects them. The W6.P history-replay check then fails, and such a release reaches Minamoto only across a W6.REL.H reset or snapshot. Keeping old keys or digests for old heights would be the height-bounded legacy path the plan forbids. The plan also never says what an Active capability does when a patch release changes its compiled digest. Either it fails closed (an outage), or it keeps accepting under a record that no longer describes the running code.

**Fix.** 1. Signer keys (owner amendment of W6.REL.K property (2)).
   - The binary pins, per production chain id, only that chain's genesis signer set. It never changes after genesis.
   - The current accepted set lives in protocol state with effective heights. It is rotated only by a transition signed by a threshold of the current set. Governance holding CanEnactGovernance cannot rotate it.
   - The W6.G verifier checks each record against the set in force at the record's height, so replay is sound across rotations without a compiled legacy key list.
   - If the owner keeps release-only rotation instead, the plan must say explicitly that every rotation release fails the W6.P history-replay check on Minamoto and reaches it only across W6.REL.H. W6.REL.H must then list signer rotation among the changes it gates, including the compromise case.

2. Compiled digest.
   - State that a release changing an Active capability's compiled capability digest changes the verifier, so W6.REL.H applies.
   - Specify the runtime rule. At each use, the verifier compares the record's digest with the running binary's digest. On mismatch the capability behaves as Suspended (fail closed, W6.RB(4) exit paths stay open) until a record with a higher sequence for the new digest is installed.

3. Tests.
   - W6.G: replay across a key rotation reproduces every certified R.
   - A release upgrade with an unchanged digest keeps the capability Active.
   - A release upgrade with a changed digest fails closed at use and resumes with a new record.
   - W6.P: a seeded rotation or digest-change candidate is flagged by the history-replay check on a recorded 4-validator export.

### F130 [critic-security] Plan §5 G4 definition (719-723), §5.1-§5.2; graph W2.3, W2.4, W2.6i, W2.Q (363-367), W6.D0.AXT, W6.R.AXT

**Problem.** G4's 'fresh issuer authorization' is silently dropped. The plan lists it as part of G4, but no field disposition, predicate step, W2 criterion, W2.6i test, review scope or W2.Q check addresses it. Anchors can be up to W blocks old and source facts are proven at the anchor. Whether an issuer authorization revoked between the anchor and inclusion is rejected is therefore unspecified, which is a guarantee narrowing with no A9 record.

**Fix.** 1. In plan §5.1 and §5.2 and graph W2.4, require that the single anchored admission path composes the issuer check (crates/iroha_core/src/state/axt_spend_issuer.rs:77-170) with the WG/D7 source resolver. That check covers issuer signatures under the current committed AxtHandleIssuerContextV1 (policy manifest root, resolved issuer key, asset incarnation, code/ABI binding), the handle counter/generation, pending-transition markers and the unconsumed issuer nonce. It runs against the current executing transaction view, never against state at the anchor. Remove its dead_code allowance.
2. Add `AxtAnchoredSpendIssuerPayloadV1.anchor` and `AxtAnchoredSpendIssuerAuthorizationV1.anchor` to the disposition table: both follow the redefined anchor, with no alias.
3. In W2.3, consume the issuer nonce (`AxtAnchoredSpendReplayKeyV1`) atomically with the source-occurrence key, budget and effects.
4. In W0.4, move AXT expiry timing (nexus.axt slot_length_ms and max_clock_skew_ms, iroha_config actual.rs:3015-3021) to protocol state, so expiry never depends on node config.
5. Add W2.6i tests. Each of these must be rejected deterministically inside R on every validator:
   - issuer authority revoked or rotated between the anchor and inclusion;
   - authority revoked by an earlier transaction in the same block;
   - authorization expired at the inclusion slot;
   - a reused issuer nonce;
   - a policy restored with equal bytes after revocation, which must not revive the old generation.
6. Add an I-checklist case for revoked or expired issuer authority.
7. Add "fresh issuer authorization (current-State authority, expiry, nonce, revocation between anchor and inclusion)" to the W6.D0.AXT and W6.R.AXT scopes.
8. Have W2.Q confirm that these tests pass on the candidate.

### F131 [critic-security] Graph A3 (57); plan §0 Networks table (69, 73), Residual trust (114-115)

**Problem.** The plan never states a residual: any chain whose id the release does not pin can install its own integration roots in genesis and activate capability code that has not been qualified. That includes third-party permissioned Iroha 3 deployments, and the code can be partial construction-stage relations shipped in the Proposed state. The residual-trust statement names only signer custody and operators.

**Fix.** 1. Add a residual to plan §0 'Residual trust', graph A3 and W6.REL.K. The text should say: on a chain id the release does not pin, the chain's own genesis may install integration roots. Those roots can activate any capability code the binary carries, including construction-stage, descoped or otherwise unqualified code. This applies to third-party or permissioned Iroha 3 deployments (specs/kagami_profiles.md:11) as well as to local integration networks. The plan's qualification guarantee covers only the pinned production-class chains.
2. Retitle the Networks-table row and W6.REL.D(2) from 'Local integration networks ... Disposable' to 'Non-pinned chains (local integration networks and third-party/permissioned deployments)'. Change their history and role to 'set by that chain's operator; no qualification guarantee'.
3. Add a W6.G test and a Torii/SDK criterion. Whether a chain's genesis carries integration roots, and which capabilities those roots activated, must be exposed as a typed, committed-state fact. The Rust, Swift and Kotlin SDKs must report it, so a client can tell a qualified activation from a self-rooted one. Rule (3) already invalidates integration roots in a genesis for a pinned production chain id, so that needs no change. The owner may instead accept this residual explicitly in W6.REL.K.

### F132 [critic-security] Plan §8.2 CA-side precondition (1339) and 'Compromised publication key' (1349)

**Problem.** The claim that a compromised publication key 'can delay a revocation only within the 300 s age cap' does not hold when the CA pre-signs staggered CRLs, which the same section allows. The publisher can keep publishing pre-signed CRLs that predate a revocation, each fresh in its own window. The delay is bounded by the pre-signing horizon, not by 300 s.

**Fix.** Make the line 1349 claim conditional, and record the horizon:

(1) Line 1349: "Under live issuance, or when future-dated CRLs are released only at their thisUpdate and withdrawn on revocation, it can delay a revocation only within the 300 s age cap. If the publisher can obtain CA-signed CRLs dated in the future, it can withhold a CRL that lists a revocation and keep rotating to earlier pre-signed ones (credentials.rs:3354-3392 checks only a larger thisUpdate and crlNumber). The delay is then bounded by min(TU_last + 301, NU_last) of the last pre-signed CRL, called the horizon H."

(2) W5.E1 (graph:462): for each CA that pre-signs, record who holds the pre-signed CRLs before their thisUpdate (CA distribution point or rotator), whether unreleased ones are withdrawn on revocation, and the horizon H.

(3) W5.D6 (graph:465 and plan 1372-1377): replace the single bound "revocation latency <= U_max + d_pub,max while the rotator is live" with a per-CA bound. For live issuance, or pre-signed CRLs released only at their thisUpdate, the bound stays U_max + d_pub,max. For a CA whose publisher holds future-dated CRLs, record H, which also covers a compromised publication key. Alternatively, W5.D1 can make release-at-thisUpdate with withdrawal on revocation part of the CA operator commitment, and mark any CA that cannot commit to it as unsupported.

(4) Update the revocation-latency bullet at line 1350 to match.

user_direction: Working RAM-LFE is mandatory, including the complete usable proof path; do not descope it or substitute signature receipts.

Remove activation gates everywhere: no Proposed/Active qualification lifecycle, qualification signer records, release-pinned capability keys, chain-ID availability switches or audit/budget activation prerequisites.

Make testnet capabilities usable incrementally as actual implementation paths land while enforcing complete mathematical proof, authentication, permission, canonicality, replicated-State and resource validity.
Use one canonical first-release V1 design. Remove legacy implementations, compatibility aliases/decoders, historical migration and old-binary matching designs.

Require deterministic restart/replay inside the current genesis epoch. Incompatible pre-release testnet changes use a fresh signed genesis through separately authorized deployment; do not promise replay of incompatible earlier history or reset a live network in this task.
Retain the existing ordinary release-signing contract and runtime-only secret custody; implementation progress is not conditioned on new approval machinery.
counting_notes: 133 counts source reports, not 133 unique defects. Each source F ID occurs exactly once as a report object.

The 30 groups are substantive root-cause families; they are not a claim that exactly 30 independent defects exist. Per-report requirements preserve distinct sub-defects, and duplicate_of is used only for repeated primary defects.
Duplicate_of does not suppress report-specific additions; overlaps_with identifies composite or partial overlaps.
Seven source reports carry FIXED (pointer); this is not full closure. F38 is explicitly partial and has substantive residual text.
Every report and group remains pending_reconciliation. Proposed supersession is distinct from a code fix or verification result.
The suggested r5 activation and compatibility remedies are not authoritative; later user instructions govern r6.
prior_reconciliation_guidance.reconciliation_guidance: All source reports are accounted for. carried_forward retains actual engineering or document-maintenance work; superseded_by_user_direction discards the old activation/compatibility premise while retaining genuine proof/auth/state obligations in r6_requirement. These suggested detail notes are subordinate to the single normative plan; they are neither a second contract nor verified fixes. No code or deployment completion is asserted.
